Together with our domestic and international partners, we aim to train 30 future experts in the RESDOC Programme.

title: Broadening Expertise for YOung Researchers iN aDvanced Cell & Gene Therapies
objective: BEYOND is a cutting-edge, International Postdoctoral Training Programme on Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products (ATMP) designed to promote excellent training through interdisciplinary, intersectoral, and cross-border mobility and collaboration. Coordinated by Fondazione Telethon (FTELE), BEYOND aims to tackle the critical skills shortage in the ATMP sector, addressing the pressing demand for intersectoral professionals capable of confidently navigating the full translational pathway of these drugs - a rapidly evolving domain at the forefront of global healthcare innovation.Over 60 months, BEYOND will recruit 35 postdoctoral researchers through 2 competitive calls, offering 3-year fellowships that blend excellent academic science with immersive exposure to all facets of the ATMP development ecosystem, tailored to meet each fellow’s interests and career goals. The Programme combines fundamental and translational research training - in cellular and molecular biology, gene and cell therapy, genomics, computational modelling and AI-protein design - complemented by tailored career development support, empowering fellows to succeed in academia and beyond.BEYOND is uniquely positioned to make a lasting impact by setting new standards for postdoctoral training: it leverages the leadership in the field of FTELE’s institutes (SR-Tiget and TIGEM), and the synergistic strengths of 3 academic implementing partners across Europe (UK, Sweden, Slovenia), alongside key associated academic/non-academic partners like EATRIS, Medicon Village, Assobiotec and Schiller & Mertens. With a holistic approach on career development, BEYOND will empower researchers to become future leaders in the ATMP field. Fully aligned with EU strategic priorities and embedded in dynamic national and regional R&I ecosystems, BEYOND supports Europe’s ambition to lead in health innovation by cultivating a critical mass of skilled scientists, ready to drive long-term scientific excellence and innovation.

title: HDFACT82: Functional characterisation of CCDC82 and its interaction with FACT in Huntington’s disease
objective: Huntington’s disease (HD) is an inherited, fatal brain disorder that causes progressive motor, cognitive, and psychiatric decline, affecting around 45,000 individuals in Europe, with no cure currently available. Although the genetic cause of HD—a CAG expansion in the huntingtin gene—is well established, patients carrying the same mutation often differ widely in age at onset, clinical presentation, and disease progression. Recent large-scale genetic studies have identified modifier genes that influence these differences, opening new therapeutic avenues. However, some of these modifiers remain poorly understood, limiting the translation of genetic discoveries into understanding of pathogenic mechanisms.HDFACT82 will deliver the first systematic characterisation of one such genetic modifier, CCDC82, and test its role in HD progression. The project builds directly on strong preliminary evidence I have generated, linking CCDC82 to chromatin regulation via the FACT complex. By combining hypothesis-driven and unbiased multi-omic approaches across cellular and animal models, together with post-mortem human brain tissue analyses, HDFACT82 will generate comprehensive datasets to uncover the biological roles of CCDC82 and define how these contribute to neuronal vulnerability and disease progression in HD, potentially paving the way for novel therapies.I will build on my PhD and postdoctoral training in molecular neurobiology, proteomics, and stem cells while working under the guidance of Prof. Jose J. Lucas, a leader in HD. His lab at the CBMSO, a top-tier research centre, offers a unique environment with state-of-the-art facilities, a dynamic scientific community, and strong translational networks. The MSCA fellowship will be crucial for advancing my scientific and transferable skills and represents a transformative step in my career, positioning me to achieve my ultimate goal of becoming an independent researcher.

title: MATERIALIZE – Methodology and Synthesis Advancement To Empower Researchers In Advanced optoeLectronIc matErials
objective: The MATERIALIZE project aims to establish a competitive, inclusive, and interdisciplinary postdoctoral training programme in advanced organic optoelectronic materials. Hosted by the Institute of Organic Chemistry of the Polish Academy of Sciences (IChO PAN), a leading European research centre in organic chemistry, MATERIALIZE will recruit 15 postdoctoral researchers through a transparent and merit-based process aligned with the European Charter & Code and HR Excellence in Research principles.The scientific focus encompasses the design and synthesis of π-extended organic compounds with tailored photophysical properties for applications in OLEDs, NIR-II imaging, circularly polarized light emitters, and molecular sensors. Despite the growing importance of such materials, progress is hindered by a critical bottleneck: limited synthetic diversity and the over-reliance on a narrow set of reactions. MATERIALIZE addresses this challenge through the development of novel synthetic methodologies that unlock new molecular architectures and functionalities. The programme integrates cutting-edge approaches, including photoredox catalysis, multicomponent reactions, electroorganic synthesis, photomechanochemistry, supramolecular chemistry, and quantum modelling of excited states.MATERIALIZE offers excellent employment conditions, individual Career Development Plans, and personalized training budgets. Fellows will benefit from a structured training programme and secondments with a strong international dimension, involving 12 academic and 3 non-academic partners across 11 countries. This network ensures broad exposure to multidisciplinary expertise and intersectoral collaboration opportunities.By combining frontier research with comprehensive and inclusive career development support, MATERIALIZE aims to empower the next generation of scientific leaders in organic optoelectronic materials and contribute to strengthening Europe's innovation capacity in light-driven technologies.

title: Predictive Maintenance Using Adaptive Domain Deep Transfer Learning: Enhancing Real-Time Fault Identification and Remaining Useful Life Prediction in CNC Machines
objective: CNC machines have become an essential part of manufacturing industries. Unfortunately, unplanned downtime due to equipmentfailure causes significant losses and disrupts production. Predictive maintenance using Artificial Intelligence (AI), particularly DeepLearning (DL), offers a solution by handling complex data, extracting hidden correlations, and predicting failures accurately. However,DL models often lack adaptability when applied to different machines or environments. Moreover, the complexities introduced by thedynamic nature of machine operations, data variability, and multiple sensors pose significant challenges to implementing thisapproach in real-time. Thus, I propose PreAdapt-CNC, a novel, robust, and adaptive AI framework incorporating adaptive domaindeep transfer learning, capable of accurately predicting component failures and remaining useful life for CNC machines underindustrial challenges. In this project, I will develop an IoT framework, a fault dataset for components, a fast signal and featureextraction algorithm, novel DL models, and perform real-time testing and validation of the designed framework. My project will havea significant economic impact by reducing unplanned downtime and increasing equipment lifespan. Furthermore, it aligns with theEU strategy for the sustainable development goal of “Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure,” boosting European industrialcompetitiveness. For the project, Prof. Dimitrios Chronopoulos, a leading expert in vibration measurement, and failure prognosis atKU Leuven, is the ideal supervisor. KU Leuven's proven track record in hosting Marie Curie fellows and managing research projects willprovide me with a cooperative environment. PreAdapt-CNC will advance my career through multidisciplinary skills, industrialexposure, and specialized training. Moreover, I will also build a long-term collaboration network with European institutes, promotingknowledge exchange, innovation, and future research.

title: Preparedness, Research and Surveillance Network for infectious Diseases in Central Africa
objective: Since 2009, EDCTP has supported regional networks of excellence to build capacity for ICH-GCP–compliant clinical trials in Central Africa. The Central Africa Clinical Research Network (CANTAM, later CACTR), coordinated by FCRM, was the first of these initiatives, and has since grown into a critical, recognized partner for multicentre research, training, and outbreak response. Over the years, additional institutions have joined, clinical trials have been conducted, regulatory and ethics bodies strengthened, and new skills embedded to attract investment in health research. Yet, the COVID-19 pandemic and recurrent outbreaks of Ebola, cholera, and mpox in the DRC, RoC, and Cameroon highlight persisting vulnerabilities: limited diagnostic capacity, workforce shortages, fragmented research systems, and weak cross-border coordination. Against this backdrop, the PRESERVE consortium will consolidate and expand regional preparedness through an integrated programme that focuses on: Expertise – Validating innovative diagnostics for TB, arboviruses, and re-emerging infections, while improving febrile illness management and clinical care. Training and capacity building – Embedding a One Health approach through INOHA, Central Africa’s first One Health institute; delivering bilingual MSc, PhD, and postdoctoral training; and strengthening mentorship and workforce development. Infrastructure – Upgrading National Public Health Laboratories, enhancing surveillance platforms, and ensuring sustainable accreditation and quality management systems. Partnerships – Deepening collaboration with Africa CDC, WHO-AFRO, CEPI, BMGF, PEPFAR, the Global Health Network, and national authorities to translate research into policy and ensure sustainability. PRESERVE builds accredited labs, open data, and skilled teams to enable rapid diagnosis, response, and a resilient, regionally owned outbreak platform with sustained impact.

title: Integrating Voltage-Driven Ionics with Magnetism for Low-Power Memory and Advanced Computing: A  Training Initiative on Energy-Efficient Information Technologies
objective: IMPACT-IT is an ambitious European Doctoral Network that addresses critical societal challenges related to energy efficiency in Information Technologies (ITs). This interdisciplinary and inter-sectoral initiative combines leading expertise in magnetism–central to modern data storage–with emerging brain-inspired ionic concepts to develop next-generation memory and computing paradigms, including neuromorphic, probabilistic, Ising, and reservoir systems. The network focuses on the design, fabrication and device integration of novel magneto-ionic materials, from thin films to complex 2D and 3D architectures. By exploiting voltage-driven ion motion to precisely tailor magnetic properties (e.g., anisotropy, coercivity, magnetization) and spin configurations (e.g., vortex states, domain walls, skyrmions), IMPACT-IT aims to significantly reduce power consumption in future IT systems. These developments align with Horizon Europe’s Green Deal objectives, coupling technological innovation with energy sustainability and paving the way toward ultra-efficient computing technologies. The consortium comprises 13 Beneficiaries and 10 Associated Partners across 10 EU Member States, the UK, and the USA, including 8 industrial partners (e.g., Singulus, SPIN-ION, Openchip, HP Enterprise) and expertise spanning Physics, Engineering, Chemistry, and Computer Science. Diversity is a priority, with 43% female PhD supervisors and co-supervisors. IMPACT-IT targets seamless translation of frontier research into real-world applications and marketable technologies. A core component of IMPACT-IT is its multifaceted training program, combining world-class research with transferable skills development (career planning, entrepreneurship, intellectual property management, etc.). Through continuous peer mentoring, the network will deliver a diverse and gender-balanced cohort of highly qualified IT specialists, capable of effectively addressing future global challenges in academia, industry, and beyond.

title: Parasite Adaptive skills and how to Counter Them
objective: Belonging to the Trypanosomatida, Trypanosoma brucei, Trypanosoma cruzi and Leishmania, the ‘tritryps’ – remain a pervasive public health threat in Africa, the Americas and Eurasia. Moreover, Leishmaniases and Chagas disease (caused by T. cruzi) are emerging infectious diseases in Europe and the USA, causing significant and increasing public health challenges in the countries affected. New and improved therapeutics and diagnostics are critical to combatting these diseases but rely on new antigens, drug targets and biomarkers being uncovered through basic research. Our aim is to establish a network that will train the next generation of researchers to develop cutting edge tools to better understand Parasite Adaptive skills and how Counter Them (PACT), through a detailed understanding of new, shared aspects of fundamental trypanosomatid biology, targeted drug screening and diagnostic development. PACT researchers will integrate into a multidisciplinary research consortium whose partners have already established academic research portfolios, with projects embedded in endemic countries, and ongoing collaborations with industrial partners. The PACT doctoral network will provide a unique research infrastructure to train 11 researchers driven to improve human health and well-being by developing the expertise to uncover and then exploit new findings in trypanosomatid biology.

title: DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe)
objective: Democracies are often perceived as inherently peaceful and resilient, yet they experience a wide range of political violence that challenges this assumption. While democratic institutions can mitigate conflict, they are not immune to riots, social unrest, extremist mobilization, or criminal violence. Moreover, democracies may erode their own legitimacy when responding to these threats through militarized security forces, emergency legislation, or repressive measures that undermine the rule of law. Understanding such dynamics requires integrating insights from fields that have traditionally evolved in parallel—democracy studies, conflict research, and comparative politics.The DIViNE Doctoral Network (Democratic Institutions and Violence Network in Europe)  unites leading European universities— Amsterdam, Essex, Milan, Madrid, and Uppsala —to train a new generation of researchers capable of analysing political violence in democratic contexts. The consortium builds on each institution’s unique strengths in quantitative conflict and behavioral analysis;  in political theory, historical methods  democratization research and in global data infrastructures and peace research. Together, they form a synergistic network that transcends disciplinary and methodological boundaries.DIViNE will provide doctoral researchers with cutting-edge training that combines large-scale data collection and computational methods with  qualitative fieldwork, historical analysis, and theory-building.  DIViNE will have four thematic work packages: WP1-Conflict inheritance and legacies in democracies; WP2- Democratization and conflict resolution; WP3- Dynamics of support for violent movements and responses; WP4-Democratic resilience and violent stress.By building a durable research infrastructure and fostering cross-national collaboration, DIViNE will position Europe at the forefront of research on how democratic institutions both constrain and reproduce political violence.

title: Integrating Circular Economy Principles into Power Transformer Fleets through Sustainable Fluid Retrofilling
objective: The project TRANSFLOW will conduct research on the topic of transformer retrofilling with alternative insulating liquids. This technique involves replacing the mineral oil (MO) in a power transformer in service with a biodegradable and less flammable liquid. According to previous research, this procedure could lead to safer and more environmentally friendly transformers with reduced fire risk, increased loading capacity, and extended lifespan. All these attributes align with the principles of a circular economy, which focuses on using minimal resources for the longest possible time while extracting maximum value from processes. However, the technique has not been adequately studied, and further research is needed to assess the impact of retrofilling on transformer operation and to evaluate the economic and technical feasibility of the method. TRANSFLOW will bring together key partners, establishing an effective and distinctive training network that combines top-tier research training with a group of academic and industrial collaborators, as well as specialized workshops focused on research and knowledge transfer. The project will develop and train a group of young researchers through critical scientific projects that push the retrofilling technique to its limits. It will shape the training delivery for the use of biodegradable and safe dielectric fluids in power substations across Europe by providing loading guidelines to determine the maximum permissible load and manage transformer overloads in retrofilled transformers; developing procedures to estimate the remaining life of a transformer that has undergone retrofilling; and equipping the recruited Early Stage Researchers (ESRs) with the skills to create tools for assessing the safety of retrofilling from thermal or dielectric perspectives, as well as providing threshold values and interpretation frameworks for the key indicators of fluid conditions in retrofilled transformers.

title: Doctoral network in green and sustainable polymers
objective: The Docgreen project brings together the research and educational expertise of six  European Universities in Green and Sustainable Chemistry with a support of an enterprise to promote the use of green methodologies in biopolymer synthesis and recycling, as well as in sustainable design. This multidisciplinary program, integrating fields such as organic and polymer chemistry, materials science, and photocatalysis, aims to green the entire modern plastics value chain. It provides doctoral students with an engaging experience, including hands-on training in diverse green techniques, knowledge integration across disciplines, and comprehensive theoretical programs offered by the institutions.   Key research areas include the greener synthesis of C5-C6 bio-based building blocks, exploration of sustainable reaction conditions— such as catalytic methods and eutectic solvents—to create new classes of polymers based on furanics, cyclodextrins and dextrins, or their combinations. The project also investigates various recycling techniques for both synthetic and bio-polymers, as well as studying new materials' functional properties and applications while assessing their sustainability.  With its extensive thematic scope, the program benefits seven doctoral candidates by exposing them to diverse academic and non academic environments, fostering mobility, and ensuring sound educational and career development through EdTech tools. This approach supports the sustainability of expertise both at the human and institutional levels, advancing knowledge and innovation that will ultimately benefit society and stakeholders, and reinforcing Docgreen’s impact within the EU and globally.

title: COllision Physics and Chemistry and its Application - Doctoral Network
objective: Charged-particle collisions with atoms and molecules are ubiquitous and underpin many natural and industrial processes, ranging from aurorae to plasma fabrication. Indeed, our understanding of such diverse phenomena as cosmic ray interactions with planetary atmospheres and surfaces, molecular synthesis in the interstellar medium, plasma generation and processing leading to material design and nanofabrication and the development of next-generation radiotherapy using ion beams, all rely upon a knowledge of collisions between electrons and ions with atoms and molecules.It is therefore vital to provide a training programme that ensures the provision of the next generation of researchers in both industry and academia with expertise in collisional phenomena and their role in physical and chemical processes. To date there is no such doctoral training programme that combines hands-on experimental research with a strong theoretical background whilst placing such research in the context of its application. With its emphasis on project-based, personal research training coupled with secondments in academia and industry and with core skills training, the COPCA-DN will deliver such a training programme that has been identified by both applied and fundamental research communities as essential to future development of their fields.The COPCA-DN brings together leading researchers and their state-of-the-art laboratories to conduct pioneering research that will deliver new data whilst simultaneously developing next-generation research facilities exploring collision physics and chemistry. The Research programme will be supported by training in both academic and transferable skills to prepare the DN’s 10 DCs for a wide range of careers across sectors in both academia and industry. The COPCA-DN formalism is thus seen to be an exemplar for wider training pan-EU programmes.

title: Soft Active Matter Microrobots for Medicine
objective: Current medical tools and robots are unable to access locations in narrow and delicate organs without highly damaging the tissues and continue suffering for lack of any flexible robot-assisted endoscope platforms that can be safely tele-manipulated for diagnosing pathologies in the ear-nose-throat districts. Microrobots, i.e. miniaturized and precisely controlled robotic devices, have the potential to overcome this issue and revolutionize medicine. To do so, however, they need to be able to sense and react to their environment, to process the information, and to generate a mechanical output controlled by external stimuli. The confined, small, hard-to-reach, and risky inner body sites discards usual engineering solutions to embody all these functionalities in microscopic devices based on standard integration approaches of sensors and actuators by assembly. Our research assumption is that a key enabler for any microrobotic solution would be the building material itself, i.e. a soft and active polymeric material, likely to adapt compliantly to narrow environments, to mechanically respond to remote stimuli, and to be shaped in the desired size and for each application. The vision driving SAM3 is therefore to develop three-dimensional miniature robots based on soft active matter which will enable novel non-invasive interventions or therapies deep inside the human body. To this aim, we are going to train a new community of young talented researchers that, starting from an understanding of the clinical needs, will be able to bridge the gaps between engineering and materials science. The doctoral candidates will receive interdisciplinary training and mentorship by academic leaders in the field of soft active materials; microrobotics and medical, and will get direct exposure to and training by clinical and industrial partners involved in the fundamental, educational, and valorisation-related aspects of the doctoral network.

title: MSCA Doctoral Network on Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer for Next-Generation Electric Mobility
objective: The BiWPT Doctoral Network (Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer for Next-Generation Electric Mobility) aims to revolutionize how electric vehicles (EVs) interact with the energy grid by developing efficient, safe, and fully bidirectional wireless power transfer (WPT) technologies. In line with the European Green Deal and Fit-for-55 objectives, BiWPT addresses the urgent need for sustainable and flexible electrification, enabling EVs to serve not only as means of transport but also as distributed energy assets that support renewable integration and reduce costly grid reinforcements.Current WPT systems are largely unidirectional and limited in efficiency, alignment tolerance, and scalability. BiWPT will go beyond the state of the art by advancing misalignment-tolerant coupling mechanisms, bidirectional converter topologies, compact shielding designs, and real-world deployment strategies compliant with international standards. The network will create fundamental knowledge and validated prototypes that enable contactless and automated vehicle-to-grid and grid-to-vehicle energy exchange, essential for the future of shared, autonomous, and electrified mobility.Through an interdisciplinary and intersectoral consortium of eight leading European universities and seven industrial partners, BiWPT will train 15 Doctoral Candidates in a combination of power electronics, electromagnetics, control, and systems integration. The program’s four scientific work packages (coupling, bidirectionality, integration, and deployment) are complemented by dedicated training and dissemination actions to realize innovation, standardization, and technology transfer.By combining academic excellence with industrial engagement, BiWPT will equip a new generation of researchers to drive Europe’s transition toward smart, wireless, and sustainable electric mobility, strengthening European leadership in power electronics and energy systems innovation.

title: Enantioselective Catalysis for Radical Transformations
objective: Asymmetric radical catalysis is an emerging frontier in chemistry, with great potential for the synthesis of chiral compounds across pharmaceuticals, fine chemicals and materials science. RADICALLY is a doctoral network designed to address timely challenges of asymmetric catalysis applied to radical chemistry by fostering a collaborative research environment spanning academia, industry and start-ups. The network integrates experimental and computational expertise in transition metal catalysis, organocatalysis and enzymatic catalysis, to train 11 doctoral candidates in cutting-edge asymmetric synthesis from every possible perspective.The research goals include the design of novel catalytic systems, the development of enantioselective radical reactions, mechanistic studies to elucidate stereocontrol pathways and the application of these methods in industrially relevant contexts. The program’s intersectoral nature ensures exposure to advanced technologies such as photoredox catalysis, electrosynthesis and AI.Industrial partners provide insights into practical applications, complementing the groundbreaking research.The proposal features five interconnected research work packages focusing on the enantioselective formation of complex targets, catalyst design, mechanistic investigations and enabling technologies for industrial integration. Projects range from asymmetric intermolecular alkenes and C-H functionalizations, to enzymatic organoboron chemistry and electrocatalysis, with secondments across partner institutions to promote interdisciplinary collaborations.RADICALLY’s “training through research” philosophy equips DCs with diverse skills, bridging academic excellence and industrial innovation, and positioning them to advance the field of asymmetric catalysis. This initiative not only aims to establish a robust framework for producing chiral molecules, but also aspires to solidify asymmetric radical catalysis as a transformative tool in synthetic chemistry.

title: Hydrogen combustion NOise Investigation for Safe and Efficient propulsion and energy systems
objective: HyNOISE is a Doctoral Network aimed to train doctoral candidates able to face current and future challenges in the prediction and control of direct and indirect noise generated by hydrogen flames. Four specific research objectives will be pursued: 1) Unveil the dynamics and sound pressure level generated during unsteady ignition and flashback process 2) Investigate the direct broadband sound generated due to the coupling between unsteady flame dynamics and flame-flame interactions, hydrodynamic and thermo-diffusive instabilities, and turbulence. 3) Understand physical mechanisms leading to the onset of thermoacoustic instabilities coupled with different modes at either with a specific focus on high frequencies 4) Study the contribution of convective waves to combustion noise and thermoacoustic instabilities. Multiple hydrogen-air archetypes typical of air-breathing hydrogen combustion systems in both single and annular multi-injector configurations will be investigated. In a collaborative partnership between academic and industry partners who are major European gas turbine manufacturers, HyNOISE bring relevant expertise together and to pursue solutions for hydrogen through integration and combination of unique and advanced theoretical, high-fidelity modelling and experimental expertise. This will lead to the development of new models and tools able to correctly predict hydrogen flame dynamics and its resulting pressure field, and, on this basis, developing control and mitigation methods to overcome current limitations in hydrogen combustion systems and design innovative, quiet, and stable combustion devices. The technologies developed will stimulate the green transition in the power generation and transport sectors, thus contributing to the achievement of the EU's challenging decarbonization goals.

title: Training program to engage flexible and disordered protein targets for therapeutic development: The oncogene β-catenin as showcase.
objective: Traditionally, proteins have been categorized into two main structural classes: ordered and disordered. Large parts of the human proteome contain intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), which are highly flexible and only sometimes adopt a distinct conformation upon interaction with a binding partner. IDRs are fundamental to intracellular signalling and protein interaction networks, particularly transcriptional regulation. Dysregulation of these processes is strongly associated with diseases including cancer and neurodegenerative disorders. However, targeting IDRs is challenging because of their dynamic nature and the lack of well-defined binding pockets. IDR targets have therefore been largely underrepresented in the pharmaceutical industry and the competencies for characterizing and targeting IDRs are lacking.The aim of the FlexCAT doctoral training network (DN) is to equip a cohort of doctoral candidates (DCs) with unique expertise and knowledge in characterizing and targeting IDRs. We aim to challenge and complement the limitations of classical small molecule approaches that were primarily developed to target druggable pockets within folded proteins. The DCs will carry out challenging research projects with the aim to assemble, expand, develop and apply novel approaches to understand and exploit disordered targets and IDRs. We will focus on utilizing β-catenin, a central therapeutic target and prime example of an IDR-related drug targeting challenge. Alongside the individual research projects, the DCs will expand their knowledge and transferrable skills through a structured training program, including secondments and contributions from the non-academic sector. The outcome of the FlexCAT DN will be increased understanding of the role of disordered targets and IDRs, their implications in disease and particularly cancer, while also developing practical strategies for exploring the therapeutic intervention of alternative IDR-related protein targets.

title: Mobile and Optical Networks for 6G (MONET-6G)
objective: The Doctoral Network MONET 6G (Mobile and Optical Networks for 6G) addresses transformative challenges in developing next-generation communication systems. As global data generation and use accelerate, the intelligent integration of mobile and optical technologies—driven by AI and emerging innovations—has become essential for achieving sustainable, high-capacity, and inclusive connectivity.MONET will bridge the physical and digital worlds through advances in optical X-haul integration, AI-native architectures, energy-efficient operations, and cyber-physical convergence. The project brings together leading academic groups and major industrial partners Ericsson, Nokia, Telefónica, and Orange, providing a multidisciplinary training platform for 12 doctoral candidates (DCs) to pioneer solutions for a secure, adaptive, and human-centred 6G networks. MONET ensures that its research outcomes are aligned with real-world application needs by fostering collaboration between academia and industry.The programme is structured around four interconnected work packages, focusing on key aspects of 6G development: high-speed/low-consumption technologies, AI-enhanced network management, joint communication and sensing techniques, and emerging user-centric applications. MONET integrates cutting-edge technologies such as digital twins, edge computing, and semantic communication to optimise spectrum use, reduce energy consumption, and support immersive services including autonomous mobility and smart cities. Sustainability and efficiency are embedded throughout the programme, targeting significant reductions in network power usage and operational complexity. Through hands-on training and industrial secondments DCs will gain direct experience in addressing real-world challenges. MONET will thus foster a new generation of innovators and research leaders, strengthening Europe’s global position in the 6G era and contributing to a resilient, intelligent, and sustainable digital future.

title: INtegration of SensInG and High performance fiber Telecommunications
objective: As both fiber-based sensing and optical telecommunications confront significant challenges in terms of performance demand, environmental responsibility and potentially reducing profit margins, the prospect of the coexistence of these technologies in combined platforms presents itself as an clear opportunity for industry, society and academia. The road for integration, though, is far from obvious.Although fiber-based sensing and optical communications share a common transmission medium, they have been developed separately from the ground up to push their individual performance boundaries without considering their eventual co-existence. This means that the constraints and requirements for the underlying technologies for each of them are often far from compatible, with exploratory research and recent tests hinting at the fact that, in most situations, co-existence would come at the cost of a great reduction in performance for one or both of the integrated applications.The goal of our proposed Doctoral Network is to use the combined expertise of our academic and industrial partners to provide a new generation of engineers and researchers with a complete vision of the design, optimisation, implementation and integration of optical fiber sensors and communication networks, their limits and their requirements in the context of current and envisioned future challenges, from the device to the system level.

title: Exploring Extended Field-of-view PET for precision medicine
objective: Recently, long axial field of view (LAFOV) PET/CT systems have been introduced in the market (more than 15 in EU) and an increasing number of systems are becoming available in Europe. These systems have an ultra-large anatomical coverage, allowing dynamic imaging covering all major organs. With a sensitivity up to 20x higher than current state of the art PET/CT, molecular imaging can now be performed with ultra-low radiation doses, allowing more repeat imaging, either for multi-radiotracer studies for comprehensive disease characterization or longitudinal studies/follow up diagnostics. This is of particular interest with the advent of novel targeted drugs and cell therapies for which there is an unmet need to achieve better in vivo phenotyping and/or characterization of disease for a more precise diagnosis as well as better understanding of drug delivery and targeting to predict treatment response. Our proposed training network, PREFERENCE, will train 15 doctoral candidates (DCs) to fully exploit the benefits of large axial FOV PET/CT imaging. The  network involves 13 PET centres, all with LAFOV PET/CT, a leading global manufacturer of LAFOV PET/CT systems and SMEs developing imaging software. Our individual research projects will develop new LAFOV methodologies to improve image quality and diagnosis, to enable studying human whole body disease connectomes, to allow for non-invasive full kinetic analysis, to facilitate low dose multi-tracer and/or multi-repeat LAFOV PET/CT imaging. Several DCs will use LAFOV PET/CT in clinical research to gain new insights and knowledge of pathophysiology and precision medicine in clinical research and patient care, increased understanding of pathophysiological processes and diagnosis for various clinical applications by using multi-tracer as well as dynamic imaging procedures. DCs will also experience a cutting-edge doctoral training programme including data analysis, artificial intelligence, innovation and entrepreneurship.

title: Circular Economy for Space
objective: The CE4Space Doctoral Network is pioneering the Circular Economy (CE) for Space, transforming the current high-risk, linear space model into one of reuse, recycling, and remanufacturing. Its ambitious research defines new satellite design paradigm with eco-design rules, develops autonomous lunar construction using regolith, achieves a new standard for collision avoidance via highly accurate, AI-enabled Space Situational Awareness, advanced robotics for in-orbit manufacturing and servicing coupled with resilient supply chains, competitive business models, regional innovation ecosystem development, geo-political risk assessment and forming of legal frameworks. It resolves fundamental, open problems in technical, economic, and regulatory Space-related domains. CE4Space will charge European space competitiveness, leading to the emergence of new space market niches and business models. The technological solutions developed will drastically reduce launch costs and the carbon footprint by avoiding materials transport from Earth. The Doctoral projects will provide crucial policy guidance on the recovery and reuse of materials in Space, safeguarding of the orbital commons, and lower the environmental impact on Earth by limiting primary raw material exploitation. CE4Space will enhance public understanding of space sustainability and champion increased inclusivity in STEM disciplines.Success is ensured through a world-class consortium of leading experts in engineering, computer science, law, and business, ensuring practical implementation of results. Its unique, multidisciplinary training program is fortified by robust joint supervision and relevant corporate secondments, cultivating the future Space CE leaders equipped with a combination of technical and transferable skills. The tailored training, anchored in ResearchComp, includes 15 unique research-based courses, 14 transferable skills courses to complement the doctoral programmes, offered by the partnering universities.

title: Multilingual Language Awareness in the European Digital Society
objective: Today’s European society faces major challenges with far-reaching implications driven by rapid digital transformation and increased mobility, such as linguistic inequality in education, the lack of linguistic diversity in academia, business and governance, the widening technology gap between well-resourced languages and less-resourced languages, biases and stereotyped language (e.g. related to gender, race) conveyed by digital tools and AI technologies. These alarming developments call for urgent action.MultiLAwa advances pluri-/multilingualism as a key driver of social cohesion and inclusion by promoting Language Awareness (LA) – the explicit and implicit knowledge of language(s) and language use – across individual, institutional and societal levels.Going far beyond existing research and doctoral training initiatives, the project’s overarching objective is to analyse the interconnections between LA, pluri-/multilingualism and digital transformation, and to translate this knowledge into practical solutions by: - investigating how LA can serve as a competence for navigating Europe’s digital transition, and how digital progress can foster LA and pluri-/multilingualism;- developing new theoretical, methodological and empirical foundations for LA in the digital age;- creating innovative digital resources and guidelines to raise LA and thus enhance pluri-/multilingualism.Bridging the gap between academia and industry, MultiLAwa brings together 10 European universities and 16 associated partners (including 11 non-academic organisations) in an exceptional multi-stakeholder consortium. MultiLAwa will train a new generation of 14 young plurilingual researchers to become experts capable of addressing language-related challenges in a rapidly digitalising society – contributing to sustainable, inclusive and pluri-/multilingual ecosystems across Europe.

title: Training Europe’s Future Leaders in AI-driven Neuro-Oncology Diagnostics and Discovery
objective: Neuro-oncology, at the crossroads of neuroscience and cancer care, plays a crucial role in treating some of the most aggressive and complex malignancies, such as glioblastomas. Despite recent advancements in research and technoloNeuro-oncology, at the crossroads of neuroscience and cancer care, plays a crucial role in treating some of the most aggressive and complex malignancies, such as glioblastomas. Despite recent advancements in research and technology, the field continues to face major hurdles in early detection, risk-adapted surgery, accurate tumour classification, and the development of effective personalized treatments, underscoring the urgent need for innovative solutions to improve patient outcomes. Current advancements in computer science, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), are revolutionizing medicine and offer unprecedented opportunities to improve areas that have historically seen limited progress, such as neuro-oncological care. However, critical gaps remain between technical innovations and their clinical application. Moreover, physicians often lack the technical background to fully utilize AI, while computer science developments may not always address clinical realities. The FutureMIND Doctoral Network aims to bridge these divides and fill in the gap of holistic experts needed to advance AI-driven diagnostics and discovery in neuro-oncology. FutureMIND brings together leading researchers, clinicians and entrepreneurs from eight countries to train 14 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) across different disciplines and sectors. By the end of FutureMIND, the DCs will be equipped to advance digital medicine as a new clinical tool to tackle brain cancers, with foreseeable impact on thousands of patients. Importantly, FutureMIND will prepare a new generation of European experts capable of addressing future challenges and of preparing the EU to sovereignly lead the digital transformation in neuro-oncology, paradigmatically for other areas of medical care.

title: Russian Influences in the European Periphery: Interdependencies, Narratives, Power
objective: Russian influence in Europe is a multifaceted phenomenon. When considering how the European Union and its Member States should manage their relations with Russia and what, if anything, ought to be done to address or counteract Russian influence in different contexts, it is important to look beyond the reductionist depictions of influence that dominate the news media. Our proposed Doctoral Network, titled INFLUENCE, intends to build knowledge of the various mechanisms, structures, and relationships that facilitate Russian influence in Europe, focusing on Europe’s strategically important Eastern periphery: the Baltic States and the Western Balkans. The INFLUENCE DN pursues this core aim through the systemic and holistic training of ten doctoral candidates by providing them with set of tools, skills and capabilities not only to successfully implement the research goal of developing a broad and innovative understanding of Russian influence in the indicated region, but also increase the potential of their career options inside and outside of academia.   The INFLUENCE DN will train excellent researchers and experts with the regional knowledge and strengthen Partner Universities to ensure continuity of high-quality doctoral training and research after the end of the project. To achieve this goal, the programme will rely on a combination of research and transferable skills training, intersectoral and international networking and extensive communication, dissemination and exploitation activities. It will consist of closely interlinked activities, allowing to achieve long-term impact on intersectoral and international knowledge circulation, increased research excellence and sustainability of collaboration between academic and non-academic organisations.

title: Mechanocatalysis for sustainable synthesis
objective: Mecat is a Doctoral Network aiming to revolutionise chemical synthesis and polymer circularity through the development of predictive, energy-efficient mechanocatalytic technologies. By integrating catalyst design, operando monitoring, data-driven modelling, and scalable processing, MECAT will establish mechanochemistry as a reliable and sustainable alternative to solvent-based transformations. The project brings together leading academic groups and industrial partners across the European value chain to create a unified scientific and technological platform capable of understanding, optimising, and scaling mechanocatalytic reactions. Fifteen Doctoral Candidates will address four core objectives: (1) design and characterisation of innovative mechanocatalysts for organic synthesis and polymer depolymerisation; (2) development of operando analytical tools to access real-time mechanistic information inside milling environments; (3) creation of predictive kinetic and process models enabling rational optimisation and digital process control; and (4) demonstration of scalable, low-energy, solvent-free processes using twin-screw extrusion, RAM technology, and pilot-scale milling systems. Environmental and economic performance will be quantified through integrated Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA).Mecat will train a new generation of interdisciplinary researchers equipped with advanced scientific, digital, and sustainability competencies, supported by a comprehensive network-wide training programme and strong intersectoral secondments. The project will deliver open, FAIR data resources, new mechanocatalytic methodologies, operando technologies, validated scale-up protocols, and comparative sustainability benchmarks. Altogether, Mecat will provide the scientific foundations and human capital needed to accelerate Europe’s transition toward safe, circular, and solvent-free chemical manufacturing, in line with the Green Deal and industrial decarbonat

title: Doctoral Network on Zinc Energy Storage Technology
objective: The ZEST project addresses global warming by advancing zinc-based battery technology, which offers a sustainable alternative to lithium-ion batteries. With global temperatures rising by 1.2°C since pre-industrial times, severe consequences like extreme weather and threats to food security have emerged. Transitioning to renewable energy sources is vital, but energy storage solutions are needed due to the intermittent nature of solar and wind power.Lithium-ion batteries, while advanced, face limitations such as reliance on scarce materials like cobalt and lithium, environmental concerns, and safety risks, including fires and toxic leaks. The ZEST project focuses on zinc-based batteries, which are more sustainable, recyclable, and safer. Zinc is abundant and has a lower environmental impact, with easier recycling processes contributing to a circular economy.Key objectives of ZEST include:- Circularity and Recyclability: Utilizing abundant and non-toxic materials, zinc batteries support a closed-loop system with up to 90% material recovery.- Battery Life Extension: Enhancing materials to prolong battery life and reduce costs.- Safety: Developing non-flammable batteries to prevent overheating.- Energy Density: Improving storage capacity for renewable energy and electric vehicles.The project involves a consortium of experts and 15 Doctoral Candidates working on interconnected research projects, aiming to improve the performance, safety, and circularity of zinc batteries. By addressing these challenges, ZEST aims to contribute significantly to a sustainable and resilient energy future. The project’s focus on novel materials, designs, and processes will push the boundaries of zinc energy storage, making it a viable and superior alternative to current lithium-ion technology. Through these efforts, ZEST seeks to support the global transition to renewable energy and mitigate the impacts of climate change.

title: Improving Drug Efficacy with next-generation AmorphouS materials and trained experts
objective: Approximately 70–90% of all new chemical entities and drug molecules under development are reported to have poor aqueous solubility. Since 2000 amorphous forms emerged as one of the most popular strategies in the pharmaceutical industry to enhance the solubility and bioavailability of challenging drugs. However, due to the intrinsic instability of amorphous materials, only a limited number of commercially available products have been developed so far by Europe’s biotech and pharmaceutical industries. Building on recent technological advances and scientific discoveries by the IDEAS partners, we are convinced that overcoming thismajor bottleneck requires a more rational approach to the elusive amorphous physical state, transcending the current empirical methods that hinder innovation. This effort demands a unified project bringing together the cross-disciplinary expertise of academic research groups in materials science, physics, chemistry, and pharmacy, alongside industry partners. The network comprises a consortium of 10 beneficiaries (7 universities, 2 large companies, and 1 SME) and 6 associated partners (1 academic and 5 industrial) from 10 EU countries. The IDEAS Doctoral Network is designed to empower a new generation of young scientists in the field of amorphous pharmaceutical systems, strengthening Europe’s biotech/pharma industry and academic innovation capacity. Through this programme, we will train 15 doctoral candidates (DCs) to address key challenges associated with amorphous materials. The fellows will collaborate to develop eco-friendly manufacturing technologies for amorphous materials, establish science-based control over material properties, and explore a wide range of materials to achieve efficient production of high-quality amorphous formulations. This advanced research-driven training will be further enriched with opportunities to develop a broad spectrum of personal, organisational, and impactful skills.

title: Remediation Enhanced by Subsurface Characterisation & monitoring Using geophysical Evaluation
objective: Across Europe, legacy and emerging contaminations continue to threaten soil and groundwater resources, degrading ecosystem services, reducing land value, and posing risks to human health. With nearly 2.8 million potentially contaminated sites, the scale of the challenge is striking. The recently adopted EU Directive on Soil Monitoring and Resilience sets the goal of achieving healthy soils across the EU by 2050. Conventional remediation practices remain challenged by the complexity and inherent uncertainty of characterising and monitoring subsurface properties and processes, and evaluating remediation performance. Europe faces a shortage of researchers and practitioners trained to apply emerging, cross-disciplinary approaches to sustainable remediation. RESCUE’s innovative doctoral training programme designed to equip doctoral candidates with the skills to integrate non-invasive geophysical methods with advanced remediation technologies responds to this need. By bridging environmental engineering with geophysics, RESCUE will strengthen Europe’s capacity to address soil and groundwater pollution challenges through more effective, efficient, and environmentally responsible solutions. Following a value-chain framework, RESCUE spans from fundamental understanding of coupled biogeochemical-geophysical processes, through high-resolution site characterisation and monitoring and optimisation of active (bio)remediation, to evaluating the socio-economic viability, sustainability and legal aspects of geophysics-informed sustainable remediation. RESCUE will drive a paradigm shift in training and practice, promoting integrated and sustainable management of soil and groundwater resources. RESCUE will train a new generation of scientists to become highly employable professionals within environmental and engineering companies, public agencies, and academic and research organizations, while establishing a sustainable training network for both academic and professional communities.

title: Initiatives to Accelerate the Translation of Research into Market-Ready Surgical Implantable Medical Devices by Strengthening Regulatory Science and Improved Regulatory Competencies Among Researchers
objective: Implant-to-Market will be a Doctoral Network (combining training and research) composed of 15 academic partners and 5 industrial partners (large companies and SMEs), focused on accelerating the translation of research into market-ready surgical implantable medical devices. Despite major scientific advances, the medical device sector, particularly implantable devices for surgery, still faces slow innovation transfer due to fragmented regulatory knowledge, limited cross-talk between scientists and regulatory experts, and shortages of skilled personnel. Training is therefore essential to reinforce innovation capacity and global competitiveness. A European doctoral network integrating training and research is the most relevant instrument to address these challenges. The training programme developed in this project will be sustained beyond the project, and the qualifications of doctoral candidates and early-career researchers will be established by the consortium using shared methodologies.The research methodology will rely on multidisciplinary and cross-sectoral collaborations involving universities, hospitals and industry. The work packages will address key needs: (i) integrating scientific data into regulatory processes and improving regulatory understanding among researchers; (ii) assessing safety and performance of implantable medical devices; (iii) reducing animal testing through alternative methods; (iv) developing multi-personalized and advanced medical devices; and (v) implementing sustainable-by-design strategies. Expected outcomes include improved regulatory-science practices, enhanced qualification pathways, accelerated translation of innovations, and stronger interaction between research, clinics, regulation and industry. implant-to-market will help bridge the gap between scientific discovery and clinical adoption worldwide.

title: Why does It Look Different? - Material Appearance International Doctoral Network
objective: Human evolution has endowed us with refined visual and cognitive skills, enabling material appearance assessment across diverse conditions and contexts. While the physics of light transport within materials is well understood, the visual mechanisms underlying perceptual equivalence among materials remain largely unexplored, and no reliable metric currently quantifies perceptual differences between them. This gap is a critical barrier to advancing aesthetic product design and manufacturing, particularly with the advent of complex designs featuring visual (color, gloss, translucency, texture) and haptic (softness, roughness) attributes made possible by new manufacturing technologies like multimaterial 3D printing. These innovations facilitate decentralized production, reducing supply chain dependence and energy consumption while enabling high-quality, customized parts, such as aesthetic dental restorations. However, current quality control methods rely on subjective visual inspection, creating variability and limiting reproducibility, especially for products requiring high appearance accuracy. To overcome this, appearance difference metrics are essential for quality control and design adjustments in line with manufacturing constraints (Appearance Gamut Mapping).Furthermore, generative AI (genAI) models in automatic product design require differentiable loss functions that capture human perception of material appearance. The WILD MAIDN project aims to establish foundational metrics for appearance difference and equivalence, advancing visual perception science and providing tools for automated, perceptually-driven design and production that can ultimately support future genAI applications.

title: A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Cultures: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia
objective: The overarching objective of the MINARET Doctoral Network (DN) programme is to contribute to global and national efforts to understand and address the challenges of promoting democratization and good governance by training the next generation of scholars equipped to explore the interconnections between law, religion, and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies. The MINARET DN is built around three interconnected goals: 1) To collect original empirical data and generate new theoretical and empirical insights into the mutually transformative interactions between law, religion, and governance in post-imperial Islamic societies. The empirical findings will enable us to engage with and advance theoretical debates in law, development and governance studies, Islamic studies, comparative political regimes, and decolonial studies. 2) To create, develop, and enhance the sustainability of doctoral training programmes focused on the study of post-imperial Islamic legal cultures. The proposed programme will integrate a variety of disciplines, sectors, fields, and geographical regions. 3) To engage with and contribute to the global democratization and good governance agenda by translating research findings into policy-relevant outputs, including workshops, conferences, peer-reviewed publications, and policy papers. The in-depth findings of the PhD projects will provide strategic intelligence and policy insights for international organizations, development agencies, decision-makers, researchers, and practitioners—both within and beyond the EU—on ways to promote democratization and good governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies. These goals will be achieved through the design and implementation of an interdisciplinary and multisectoral DN programme on the sociology of post-imperial Islamic legal cultures, involving 15 doctoral candidates, each pursuing a PhD at one of the 11 leading European universities that form part of the MINARET consortium.

title: Doctoral Training Network for Design of Resilient Systems-on-Chip
objective: Reliable electronics is essential in safety- and mission-critical domains, such as space missions, aviation, automotive, wireless communications, data centers, healthcare, automated industry. With increase in complexity of Integrated Circuit (ICs), advancement in semiconductor technology and evolving market trends and application requirements, the IC design paradigm is shifting from classic “reliable systems” to “resilient systems”. A resilient IC has the ability to monitor its own state, detect and predict faulty scanarios, and perform self-reconfiguration/self-healing to maintain the required functionality. Besides ensuring enhanced reliability and safety, resilient systems aim to provide a balance between performance, fault tolerance and power consumption, resulting in extended system lifetime.Given the strategic goal of EU to enhance its capacities in semiconductor domain (European Chips Act), as well as the shortage of highly skilled personnel for IC design, there is an urgent need for creating a new generation of skilled experts for ICs design. As the demand for safety- and mission-critical applications is projected to increase in coming years, particularly with new space missions and adoption of 6G wireless communications across numerous domains, special attention should be given to boosting the European capacities in the design of resilient Systems-on-Chip (SoC). The RESYST-CHIP project will train 15 highly-skilled and entrepreneurially-oriented researchers in the design of resilient SoCs. The project brings together 20 leading research institutes, universities and companies, with the aim to address synergistically the critical challenges in 4 research domains - reliability characterization and modeling, CAD tools for resilience-by-design, on-chip sensing and analytics, and design of resilient architectures. The RESYST-CHIP network will employ a comprehensive training program combining complementary scientific and transferrable skills training.

title: Ecodesign Doctoral Network
objective: The way domestic and industrial products and their business models are designed will, to a large extent, define the long-term prospects for our planet and the well-being of future generations. In the shorter term, it will also heavily impact the competitiveness and resilience of the EU economy. Therefore, the ECODESIGN Doctoral Network (DN) has a critical mission: to train a new generation of product (eco)design and associated impact-assessment experts. With the recently approved Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) and the ongoing revision of the End-of-Life Vehicle (ELV) directive,  as well as the Circular Economy Action plan and Critical Raw Materials Act, the European Commission (EC) has set ambitious ecodesign targets. To support the realisation of these targets, new ecodesign technologies, as well as methods, tools, guidelines, and associated assessment methods, will be investigated for the most precarious product groups containing Critical Raw Materials (CRMs) in the electrical, electronic, and automotive sectors. ECODESIGN DN will consider a holistic, future-oriented full-product lifecycle perspective that accounts for all impacts on Planet, People, and Prosperity (3P) to propose requirements that bridge product, waste, and other horizontal EU policies. For this, ECODESIGN will conduct research into new designs to enhance AI-supported human-robot cooperative reuse, repair, remanufacturing, and recycling (WP1). This will be integrated into ground-breaking, information-exchange technologies in line with the concept of the Digital Product Passport (DPP) (WP2). To assess how the adoption of these designs and technologies will contribute to the United Nations’ (UN) Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), new methods for assessing environmental (WP3), social (WP4), and economic (WP5) impacts will be developed. Training materials (WP6) will be publicly shared, along with the developed methods and tools, on an online platform (WP7).

title: Doctoral network on discovering pathomechanisms and novel drug optimization for AMD
objective: PANDORA will create a multidisciplinary, intersectoral European Doctoral Network focusing on complement system-mediated pathomechanisms and therapy development for Age-related macular degeneration (AMD). AMD, major cause of blindness in the elderly population, affects daily activities of ca. 200 million people worldwide, placing a major burden on national health systems and impairing patients’ quality of life. The complement system, known for its role in innate immune surveillance, is a major pathogenic driver in AMD, also involved in various other diseases, including sepsis, neurodegenerative, kidney, vascular diseases and cancer. We and others have recently demonstrated the importance of locally produced complement factors and non-canonical complement functions in the retina, affecting energy metabolism, protein degradation, mitochondrial stability, autophagy and lysophagy, which are found to be impaired in AMD. PANDORA will exploit state-of-the art model systems and techniques, including ex vivo multicellular, stem-cell derived and murine models, omics, imaging, biochemistry, histology, functional assays and computational modelling, to study in depth the different complement functions relevant to AMD and to find potential biomarkers for stratification and disease monitoring. PANDORA further aims to develop innovative therapeutic approaches, using gene therapy, compound screening, optimizing drug delivery to the retina, and a novel ultra-high resolution multimodality imaging system to monitor disease progression and treatment efficacy in vivo and in patients. PANDORA will train Doctoral Candidates as the next generation of European translational scientists in vision and medical research, and provides every student with the tools for a successful scientific career in academia or industry. Our multidisciplinary network offers a unique opportunity to expand the understanding and therapeutics for AMD in Europe, and to bring research findings to benefit for patients.

title: Lectin ligands for modulation of immunity
objective: LLIMIT (Lectin LIgands for Modulation of ImmuniTy) is a European doctoral training network dedicated to advancing immunomodulatory glycoscience. The network aims to equip a new generation of researchers with the skills to design and develop ligands that target immune-related lectins - an innovative, yet under-explored therapeutic strategy against immune disorders, which are among today’s major global health challenges.The consortium unites seven academic institutions with accredited PhD programmes in organic and medicinal chemistry, structural biology, immunology and pharmacology, each with strong expertise in glycoscience. They are joined by six non-academic partners and a graduate and research academy, ensuring comprehensive, cross-sector training that spans fundamental science, translational research, and entrepreneurship.Key objectives of LLIMIT include:•Recruiting and training 14 doctoral candidates in a joint research-based programme supported by expert supervision and specialised training events.•Advancing innovative research on immune lectins and carbohydrate ligands, covering the full early drug discovery pipeline, from target identification and validation to advanced glycochemistry, drug design, and hit and lead discovery.•Establishing a sustainable foundation for European excellence in glycodrug and immunomodulatory research.•Developing a common glycodrug curriculum across participating institutions to standardise and strengthen education in this field.•Building and maintaining long-term partnerships that ensure continuity in training, research, and innovation well beyond the project’s duration.By achieving these goals, LLIMIT will bridge the gap between Europe’s outstanding glycoscience research and the urgent need for novel glycodrugs.

title: Advanced MOnitoring for a Resilient Environment (AMORE) – Nano sensing and Advanced Hybrid Modelling for PFAS, Micro- and Nano-plastics, and Pathogens detection in water.
objective: Ensuring water quality and safety requires effectively detecting emerging contaminants, which present significant risks to both human health and the environment. Current sensing technologies for detecting emerging contaminants are under research and continuously developing. Still, critical barriers exist to their implementation and use, such as high costs, lack of reliability, and difficulties in implementation in real world. Moreover, the environmental detection of several emerging contaminants like PFAS, microplastics and pathogens is still a challenge due to their complex nature (PFAS, pathogens), chemical inertness (MPs, NPs), and their high dilution rates in the environment (MPs, NPs, pathogens). The AMORE Doctoral Network will comprise 15 Early Career Researchers who will pursue these challenges by gaining scientific knowledge and advanced skills to significantly advance in environmental monitoring of challenging emerging contaminants in the aquatic environment. Four scientific objectives set the foundation of this ambitious network.      1) improve the knowledge of sensing PFAS in water samples’ environmental context,      2) design sensing strategies for the detection of micro- and nano-plastics (MPs&NPs) in water sources,      3) develop novel functionalised interfaces for selective detection of water parasitic and bacterial pathogens,     4) create advanced modelling tools for predictive monitoring of environmental emerging contaminants.8 world-leading research teams with expertise in analytical chemistry (ICRA), chemical sensing (DCU Water Institute), sensing technologies (TYNDALL), microbiology and parasitology (USC), nanomaterials (UBA, CNR), and advanced modelling (URJC, UU) from 5 countries (Ireland, Italy, Spain and the United Kingdom) have joined efforts to create this proposal. AMORE aims to produce significant advancement in sensing PFAs, MPs and NPs, cryptosporidium and bacteria in water, focusing on relevant EU and UK case studies.

title: Doctoral Network on Intelligent Laser Precision Manufacturing
objective: Laser-based precision manufacturing is a critical technology for Europe’s competitiveness, enabling high-value applications in microelectronics, photonics, and medical devices. However, its industrial adoption remains limited due to the complexity of laser material interactions and the lack of real-time process monitoring and adaptive control. INTELLASE addresses these challenges by laying the foundations for first-time-right intelligent laser micro and nanomanufacturing systems. The project focuses on three core objectives: innovative process design, real-time multimodal monitoring, and adaptive process control, combining physics-based modelling, advanced sensing, and AI-driven decision-making.The objective of INTELLASE is to develop an interdisciplinary European network to train 15 doctoral candidates (DC) in laser-material interaction physics, photonics engineering, sensing- and modelling-powered intelligent control, enabling them to support and advance the development of next-generation laser-based micro-/nanomanufacturing systems. INTELLASE brings together a consortium of 20 partners from eight countries, including eight leading universities, two research centres, and ten industry actors, covering the full industrial ecosystem: laser system integrators, optical component designers, sensor developers, digitalisation providers, and end users. This structure ensures rapid transfer of research outcomes into industrial practice.The doctoral candidates will be equipped to design and deploy intelligent laser manufacturing solutions that enable sustainable, high-throughput production and strengthen Europe’s leadership in advanced manufacturing. INTELLASE will deliver transformative technologies and a highly skilled workforce, creating significant scientific, economic, and societal impacts across strategic sectors.

title: Transport resilience against natural and anthropogenic disruptions
objective: The TRANSCEND Doctoral Network focuses on strengthening the resilience of transport infrastructure against both natural andhuman-induced disruptions. It addresses global challenges such as extreme weather events, resource scarcity, and geopoliticaluncertainties, aiming to transform how transport systems are planned, operated, and maintained. By bringing together topacademic institutions, industry leaders, and governmental organizations from across Europe and beyond, TRANSCEND combinesadvanced research, interdisciplinary collaboration, and practical applications to develop innovative solutions. The program will train14 Doctoral Candidates (DCs) through a structured curriculum that focuses on mitigation, adaptation, sustainability, and governancestrategies. The key objectives of TRANSCEND are:- Designing risk-based frameworks integrating digital twin technologies for predictive maintenance of roads, railways, and ports.- Advancing sustainability by optimizing the use of low-carbon materials and integrating lifecycle thinking.- Developing dynamic response strategies for evacuation and recovery during crises.- Enhancing urban mobility by addressing vulnerabilities and fostering adaptive planning and design.TRANSCEND utilizes tools such as hazard modelling, vulnerability analysis, system dynamics, and machine learning to addressshortcomings in current resilience approaches. The program integrates expertise from various disciplines, including materials science,environmental engineering, social sciences, and digital technologies. By prioritizing open science, interdisciplinary training, andcollaboration with industry, TRANSCEND, besides tackling current challenges, it ensures the long-term resilience of transportsystems. The initiative aligns with key global policies, including the European Green Deal and the UN Sustainable Development Goalsand prepares a new generation of researchers to drive advancements in resilient infrastructure.

title: Data Science and Genomics Training for Chronobiology in Mental Health
objective: DataGenChrono brings together 12 international partners from eight countries—world-class experts in human genomics, data science, sleep, chronobiology, strategic science communication and career development—to advance understanding of the genetic foundations of sleep and circadian biology in mental health. The network will train 11 Doctoral Candidates, forming an excellent, collaborative cohort of researchers who will discover the biological bases of mental health addressing disorders that are a major public health challenge in Europe and worldwide. The research programme objectives of DataGenChrono are to:1) Identify novel genetic influences on sleep and circadian dysfunction linked to poor mental health across populations and diagnostic groups.2) Uncover causal relationships between sleep/circadian dysfunction and mental health symptoms across the lifespan. 3) Apply cutting-edge data science, sleep/activity monitoring, and genetically informed approaches to develop novel pathways for sleep and circadian interventions in clinical care and public health.4) Enhance international engagement, visibility and impact through coordinated dissemination, outreach, and stakeholder partnerships, ensuring findings reach scientific, clinical, policy and public audiences. The DataGenChrono programme provides excellent, interdisciplinary research projects within highly attractive institutional environments.Candidates will gain- world-class scientific training- exposure to diverse research and future workplaces- embedded engagement, career development, transferrable skills and networking opportunities across Europe and worldwide.From recruitment to graduation, the DataGenChrono programme ensures the highest-quality PhD training and excellent science, fostering a connected, high-performing cohort that will leave a lasting contribution in both research and the wider community, fully aligned with the European Commission’s Principles for Innovative Doctoral Training.

title: Building Europe’s Internet Resilience for a Connected Future
objective: Europe’s digital sovereignty depends on communication infrastructures that remain secure, resilient, and interoperable across land, sea, and space. Today, these systems face escalating risks: fragile submarine cables, concentrated Internet interconnection markets, limited satellite access, and cyber-physical threats that move across domains. RESILIOUS addresses these challenges by establishing a pan-European Doctoral Network to develop resilient-by-design architectures, detection methods across all domains, recovery techniques, and evidence-based governance frameworks.The network brings together leading academic and industrial partners to advance four research pillars: (1) new metrics and architectures; (2) multi-layer anomaly detection; (3) autonomous recovery via reinforcement-learning routing, passive localisation, and degraded-mode communication for terrestrial and maritime systems; and (4) certification, standardisation, and regulatory tools supporting EU-wide resilience and strategic autonomy.Fifteen Doctoral Candidates will receive interdisciplinary training spanning satellite and terrestrial networking, underwater sensing, security, Internet governance, and techno-economics. Through secondments with operators, vendors, and international organisations, they will gain hands-on experience with real infrastructures and standardisation processes.RESILIOUS will deliver validated resilience metrics, interoperable designs, cross-domain detection and recovery demonstrators, and policy instruments aligned with EU directives. The project builds the scientific foundations and skilled workforce required to ensure robust, sovereign, and future-proof connectivity for Europe.

title: Training Network on Quantum Electrodynamics with Silicon NanoTechnology
objective: Quantum technologies (QT) have the potential to revolutionize computing, communication, and sensing, and recent advances in silicon nanofabrication have created a unique opportunity for realizing a new class of quantum electrodynamical (QED) technologies, which exploit quantum vacuum fluctuations in solid-state systems at the deep nanoscale. The potential for developing unprecedented nanomechanical and nanophotonic quantum devices is immense, but the necessary interdisciplinary and intersectoral frameworks are currently missing at the international and European levels. The QUEST Doctoral Network aims to overcome these limitations by establishing a world-class training and research programme that unites leading European academic institutions, research centres, and industrial partners across all necessary disciplines. QUEST will train 15 doctoral candidates (DCs) to advance the science and technology of silicon QED, thereby making significant contributions at the intersection of three areas of key strategic importance for Europe: semiconductor nanotechnology, photonics, and quantum technology. The combined program will develop the material and fabrication technology, the measurement tools, and the necessary conceptual and theoretical models to exploit the opportunities offered by silicon QED at the deep nanoscale.
