By combining complementary expertise and fostering cross-sector mobility, the network will educate a new generation of DCs in the full stack of skills needed in silicon quantum photonics technologies, including theory, modelling, design, material growth, nanofabrication, and a wide range of experimental techniques - as well as communication, collaboration, and leadership skills - which are all key elements for the success of the Quantum Europe Strategy, the EU Chips Act, and the long-term competitiveness and sovereignty of the European semiconductor and QT sectors.

title: ELLE: European Doctoral Network on Secure and Safe Artificial Intelligence in the Age of Foundation Models
objective: ELLE proposes a European doctoral network aimed to train a new generation of AI scientists and professionals that will promote and reinforce the European leadership in the development of secure and safe AI technology. Within ELLE, we will tackle four main scientific and technical challenges that are hindering the concrete implementation of legally-compliant AI models with the provisions of the EU AI Act and related regulations, especially after the recent paradigm shift that has fostered the wide adoption of foundation models. These challenges include ensuring the main trustworthiness properties of learning algorithms, i.e., (i) technical robustness and safety; (ii) privacy and data governance; and (iii) interpretability and transparency; while considering models that can be (iv) continuously adapted in security-sensitive and safety-critical tasks where the data is streaming, non-stationary and showing unexpected changes of its statistical characteristics. ELLE aims to tackle these challenges jointly, building upon three main pillars: (1) the proposal of 15 distinct, multi-disciplinary Ph.D. research programs that are deeply intertwined within the four aforementioned challenges via carefully defined co-supervisions and secondments; (2) the development of open courses, educational material, and workshops, with an emphasis on hands-on, collaborative learning and attention to transferable skills; and (3) the promotion of mobility and knowledge transfer; all within a training network that includes a selection of Europe's finest researchers, supported by the ELLIS Society and stemming from the ELSA European Network of Excellence. ELLE will integrate novel and rigorous science developments with training skilled doctoral researchers to nurture and sustain the development and deployment of AI technology in compliance with the EU AI Act and related regulations, serving and promoting foundational EU values.

title: Sanctions Effectiveness Network for Scholarship and Evaluation through Interdisciplinarity
objective: The sanctions imposed on Russia and the debate that followed have reminded us how little we know about sanctions effectiveness and how wide the gap remains between theory, which often concludes that sanctions do not work, and practice, where sanctions are used more frequently than ever. SENSEI addresses this gap by building the first integrated European research and training network dedicated to understanding how sanctions function across their entire policy cycle.The objectives of SENSEI are to develop a coherent interdisciplinary framework for analysing sanctions, to create practical tools that support evidence based policymaking, and to train a new generation of specialists capable of evaluating sanctions from legal, political and economic perspectives. These objectives will be achieved through the coordinated training of 12 Doctoral Candidates who will work across universities and think tanks specialized in international affairs. Their work will contribute to two shared outputs: an EU Sanctions Toolkit for practitioners providing a structured approach to assessing sanctions design, implementation and impact, and a Sanctions Theory Handbook that consolidates conceptual insights into sanctions success and failure. Individual projects will address key stages of the sanctions cycle, supported by secondments, joint workshops and close engagement with practitioners.SENSEI is fully aligned with the aims of the Marie Skłodowska Curie Actions by offering high quality doctoral training, fostering interdisciplinary and intersectoral cooperation, and strengthening links between academia, civil society and policy institutions. It also responds to the EU’s strategic need for improved analytical capacity in a rapidly evolving policy domain. In addition, SENSEI will improve how private sector actors navigate the complexities of sanctions implementation, reducing compliance costs and enhancing overall effectiveness through better coordination with public authorities.

title: European doctoral network for proofreading the proteome
objective: Targeted Protein Degradation (TPD), an innovative strategy to redirect the cellular degradation machinery towards the elimination of disease-relevant proteins, has attracted enormous attention from researchers, industry and clinicians. TPD is based on the capacity of a small molecule, the degrader, to re-route the ubiquitination machinery towards a selected protein of interest to trigger its ubiquitination and degradation by the Ubiquitin Proteasomal System, via its interaction with specific E3 ubiquitin ligases.ProofReading will bring together a diverse community, assembling the necessary multidisciplinary expertise to develop novel TPD approaches applicable to various cellular and disease contexts, facilitating the generation of degraders. ProofReading will establish an interdisciplinary, intersectoral and international research programme to drive the development of tools, degraders and innovative strategies aimed at eliminating targets involved in cancer, infection, inflammation and rare diseases.The network comprises 10 universities, 4 research centres and 8 innovative companies, which will provide state-of-the-art training for the recruited Doctoral Candidates (DCs). This is the only doctoral network related to proteome proofreading by using TPD that combines the knowledge in all disciplines, ranging from life to physical sciences, required to develop a degrader. Interdisciplinary and intersectoral secondments will expose the DCs to different working environments. We will organize 5 hands-on research workshops on central methodological and technical aspects of TPD and 7 courses on transferable skills, of primary importance for increasing the employability of the DCs. We will also address the important issue of mental health and well-being in science.ProofReading will train 11 researchers with specific knowledge in the cutting-edge technology of TPD, which will contribute to the generation of future drugs to treat diseases.

title: Green Light for Advanced Solutions in Stained Glass Conservation and Application of Research and Education
objective: Glass-Care addresses the need to safeguard Europe’s stained-glass heritage, which is rapidly deteriorating due to pollution, climate fluctuations and the decline of traditional restoration skills. These iconic artworks, central to European cultural identity, remain insufficiently documented and increasingly vulnerable. Current conservation approaches often depend on destructive sampling and lack standardised, sustainable methods. Glass-Care goes beyond the state of the art by integrating portable spectroscopy, advanced imaging, green chemistry and digital infrastructures. The project introduces innovative technologies, photoacoustics, ptychographic microscopy and multimodal tomography, together with eco-friendly cleaning and reconstruction protocols, predictive deterioration models and a digital twin stained-glass window model. These advances will enable real-time condition assessment, long-term monitoring and environmentally responsible conservation strategies. Through an ambitious MSCA Doctoral Network, Glass-Care trains 15 doctoral candidates in an international, interdisciplinary and intersectoral environment. Fellows will combine hands-on research with thematic schools and transferable-skills development, gaining expertise in cutting-edge analytical techniques, sustainable materials and advanced data processing. They will be equipped to become future leaders in heritage science and conservation. Glass-Care’s impact is far-reaching: it will deliver 15 end-user protocols, 4 demonstrator set-ups, 2 reference databases and 3 digital infrastructures to ensure uptake by museums, conservators and educators. By aligning technological innovation with sustainability and education, the project strengthens Europe’s leadership in cultural-heritage preservation, supports the Green Deal and multiple SDGs. Its outcomes will enhance Europe’s capacity to protect stained-glass windows and ensure that conservation practice evolves with environmental pressures and societal needs.

title: Doctoral Training in Ruminant Microbiome Science:Developing Evidence-Based Interventions for Sustainable Food Production and Climate Change Mitigation
objective: RUMEN-INNOVATE will establish a pioneering Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network that advances sustainable ruminant agriculture through microbiome-based innovations. Building on extensive existing datasets, this network will train the next generation of scientists to revolutionise direct-fed microbial applications and sustainable ruminant production.The programme operates through three integrated pillars: Discovery & Prediction using machine learning and multi-omics to identify key microbiome-host interactions; Validation & Mechanistic Understanding through controlled studies and synthetic microbial community design; and Translation & Implementation developing real-world diagnostic tools, delivery systems, and on-farm technologies.RUMEN-INNOVATE will train doctoral candidates across European institutions with industry partnerships spanning nutrition companies, dairy, and meat sectors. Researchers will gain expertise in computational biology, experimental validation, and commercial application—creating versatile scientists capable of bridging laboratory discovery with agricultural implementation.The network addresses critical global challenges: feeding a growing population sustainably, reducing greenhouse gas emissions from livestock, and developing alternatives to antibiotics in animal agriculture. By advancing microbiome-based solutions, RUMEN-INNOVATE will deliver innovations that enhance animal health, improve production efficiency, and support environmental sustainability.Through international, interdisciplinary, and intersectoral collaboration, the network will produce breakthrough technologies, highly skilled researchers, and direct pathways for microbiomics innovations to reach farmers and consumers, positioning Europe as the global leader in ruminant microbiome science.

title: Using science-driven response diversity knowledge to leverage efficient ecosystem preservation and restoration
objective: Ecosystem resilience is the capacity of an ecosystem to withstand natural and human-induced changes while maintaining core functions over time and space. Response diversity (RD)—the variability in responses to environmental changes among ecosystem components—is a crucial mechanism underpinning ecosystem resilience. By enhancing adaptive capacity, RD contributes to ecosystem stability and long-term functionality. Despite this, RD remains insufficiently understood and underutilized in ecological management, conservation, and policy design. Researchers have identified several critical uncertainties that hinder the scientific advancement and practical application of RD. In addition, and perhaps due to the research gaps, despite a wide consensus of RD’s importance for ecosystem resilience, RD is often overlooked in policy frameworks, restoration practices, and monitoring and management schemes.  ReDiLEEP aims to close these gaps by establishing an interdisciplinary Doctoral Network. By conducting cutting-edge research and equipping doctoral candidates with specialized expertise, ReDiLEEP will catalyse long-term advancements in ecosystem resilience and management. In particular, the program will  -build theoretical foundations - develop measurable approaches - connect research to practice. ReDiLEEP will serve as a pivotal initiative, creating a robust science-policy-practice interface that firmly establishes RD as a cornerstone of ecosystem resilience. The program employs an integrated approach, empowering doctoral candidates with a comprehensive learning experience that spans theoretical, empirical, and practical domains. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, ReDiLEEP bridges critical gaps between ecological research, policy design, and practical application. Furthermore, participants will actively contribute to transformative change by aligning their work with the EU Biodiversity Strategy for 2030 and supporting the objectives of the UN Decade on Ecosystem

title: A Doctoral Training Network on the Study Of Premodern Ceramic Heritage: Integrating Experimental and AI-Enhanced Interdisciplinary Research
objective: SOPHIA-DN is a doctoral network that uses ceramics, the most widespread and informative form of material heritage, to investigate how craft traditions emerged, evolved, and connected cultures across the ancient world. It unites leading European scholars and institutions in a unique alliance offering advanced training and innovative research through an experimental approach. Material experimentation is central to reconstructing and testing ancient techniques, showing how past societies advanced technologically, overcame production challenges, and sustained long-term traditions. SOPHIA-DN stresses that such achievements were cumulative, intergenerational knowledge rooted in enduring practices. These embodied tacit wisdom (sophia in Greek), reflecting deep familiarity with raw materials, processes, and tools refined through centuries of observation and repetition. By highlighting this human dimension, the project emphasises the intellectual depth and cultural continuity of ceramic production, treating traditions as living repositories of experiential knowledge. The network integrates material characterisation and archaeological interpretation with hands-on engagement across the chaîne opératoire, testing observations through data-driven experimental reconstruction. In parallel, it employs digital humanities and artificial intelligence to process and link large datasets of material, technological, and cultural information. AI-assisted pattern recognition and machine learning unlock new analytical potential, redefining how ceramic legacies are studied and communicated. This integrated experimental–digital framework enables doctoral fellows to test hypotheses on archaeological artefacts while developing innovative methods of data integration and interpretation. Spanning Europe, the Eastern Mediterranean, North Africa, and the Arabian Gulf, SOPHIA-DN explores understudied ceramic technologies and contributes to reshaping how ancient history and archaeology are understood.

title: Empowering Human Agency in AI-Augmented Futures of Work
objective: The EMANAIRE network will train 15 doctoral fellows to study and shape the augmented organisation - workplaces in which agentic and generative AI changes how people decide, collaborate and build capability. EMANAIRE embeds comparative longitudinal research in eight European countries and examines different organisational settings, including public administration, technology, manufacturing, and creative industries. It responds to a practical question: how to design, govern and implement augmentation so that strategy, everyday work and long-term capability co-evolve. The programme targets four interlocking tensions in responsible AI integration: top-down governance; bottom-up workflow change; social distribution and team dynamics; and temporal consequences for skills and careers. The doctoral network will study how leadership practices and decision structures adapt, how AI systems become embedded in workflows, how augmentation affects dependencies and team collaboration, and it will trace shifting skill requirements to produce clearer maps of emerging role families and career pathways. Results will be translated into empirically grounded guidance, such as diagnostic tools, practical recommendations and capability frameworks. These will be developed in collaboration with employers, unions and public bodies. Training brings together advanced empirical methods, human-centred design, socio-technical analysis and intersectoral secondments, all supported by a shared measurement strategy and transparent research practices. Through comparative studies, multi-level instruments and longitudinal data, the network will generate governance models, workflow insights, indicators of team interaction, and evidence on career development that can be applied across sectors. EMANAIRE aligns with European priorities on trustworthy, human-centred AI and contributes to the UN SDGs on decent work and industry, graduating researchers for trustworthy, inclusive and sustainable augmentation.

title: Embodied Multimodal Human Communication and Modelling
objective: The EMHCAM Doctoral Network will train 15 doctoral candidates to advance European research in Embodied Multimodal Human Communication And Modelling. Despite rapid progress in language and vision AI, current systems lack grounding in the embodied and context-dependent nature of human communication. This limits progress in key application domains such as socially interactive agents, accessibility technologies and health-related human–machine interaction. EMHCAM addresses this gap by integrating three research communities — gesture and cognitive interaction studies, multimodal corpus development and multimodal data science — into a single, coherent doctoral training network.The network tackles three interconnected scientific challenges: 1) developing new theoretical accounts of how speech and gesture jointly structure communication across languages, speaker profiles and interaction settings; 2) creating the next generation of embodied multimodal corpora, linking audio–visual and motion-captured data with shared annotation conventions and making them available through ethical data-sharing methods; 3) designing computational models that analyse and generate multimodal behaviour, including LLM-based generation pipelines and context-aware behavioural modelling.The resulting resources — open multimodal datasets, validated annotation schemes, evaluation benchmarks and ethically robust modelling pipelines — will have concrete impact across academia and industry. Application areas include intelligent hearing aid design, socially interactive agents for mental healthcare and multimodal learning technologies. By combining advanced technical training, strong industry participation and an interdisciplinary, cross-European research environment, EMHCAM will produce a new generation of researchers equipped to shape human-centred, trustworthy and inclusive multimodal technologies in line with European strategic priorities.

title: The doctoral network for cell METAbolism and MORPHology interplay in cortical malformation-associated neurodevelopmental disorders
objective: Studying the interplay between cell metabolism and cell morphogenesis is a new, important entry point to unravel understudied mechanisms regulating human brain evolution and potential causes of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). The ambitious METAMORPH Doctoral Network (DN) will be an interdisciplinary platform for doctoral candidates (DCs), aiming to provide high quality education and training, and to promote optimal standards of research integrity, while achieving excellence in research. To accomplish the goal of METAMORPH, 6 highly qualified academic partners and 2 industrial partners from 4 countries (Finland, France, Germany and Italy) have teamed up to address the following scientific objectives: to determine the role of cell METAbolism and cell MORPHogenesis interplay in i) human cortical development, ii) the aetiology of NDDs), and iii) human neocortical evolution, by exploiting the complementary expertise and strengths of the teams. Our network will bring together not only top-notch training to provide DCs with an opportunity to METAMORPHose into world-class, leading scientists, but also advanced knowledge to improve diagnostic strategies and identify potential druggable targets for NDDs.

title: Metabolic disease heterogeneity definition, prevention and remission with targeted interventions
objective: Obesity, diabetes and associated complications constitute a rapidly escalating scientific and societal challenge across Europe marked by profound heterogeneity in causes, clinical trajectories and treatment responses. This heterogeneity explains the limited effectiveness of standardized therapies and highlights the need to stratify metabolic disease. To confront this challenge, MEDIculous REMeDy brings together a pan-European, interdisciplinary doctoral network spanning academia, healthcare, industry, public and patient organizations. The network’s first objective is to train critical and entrepreneurial metabolic health researchers through innovative interdisciplinary, translational and intersectoral training focused on tailored career development, transferable skills and leadership. Gender-responsive research design, open science, public and patient engagement underpin this training culture, equipping DCs with essential skills for academic and non-academic careers.  These early-career researchers will drive – and be shaped by – our scientific objectives: (1) to map metabolic disease heterogeneity across the full disease spectrum from early metabolic dysfunction and obesity to advanced diabetes with complications, and (2) to dissect this heterogeneity from underlying molecular mechanisms to biomarkers, therapeutic targets and treatment responses. To achieve its scientific objectives, the consortium will integrate metabolic medicine and computational systems biology that draw on multi-country European patient cohorts, advanced human in vitro platforms and complementary in vivo disease models. This novel integrative strategy enables the development of robust patient stratification and personalized therapeutic approaches applicable across European populations, pushing precision medicine forward. By uniting scientific excellence, pioneering training and societal relevance, MEDIculous REMeDy transforms metabolic disease research and precision medicine across Europe.

title: Developing Immune Strategies to Counter  tumor-immune-micrOnVironmEntal Resistance in NeuroEndocrine Tumors.
objective: Despite significant investments of resources, policies, global partnerships and social and financial efforts in the fight against cancer, we are currently still unable to achieve long-term disease control for patients with neuroendocrine tumors (NET). Moreover, despite the emphasis of both Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan and the European Initiative on Rare Cancers on advancing research and innovation in rare tumors, only limited progress has been made in the field of NET over the last decade. Particularly, the transformative waves of immunotherapy success across oncology have not yet reached NET. By bringing together experts in NET biology, pioneers in immuno-oncology research, clinicians from NET expert centers, patient advocates, and representatives of the public health sector, dIscOverNET will lead to outstanding interdisciplinary and intersectoral research. This dynamic and synergistic collaboration, will explore the potential of leveraging the immune system for the treatment of NETs, which might be able to induce durable anti-tumor responses and cure NETs. Through a comprehensive, multidisciplinary training program aligned with European doctoral training principles, the dIscOverNET doctoral candidates will be equipped to take on leading roles in European industry, academia, or government.

title: Equitable musculoskeletal health driven by inclusive models
objective: Musculoskeletal (MSK) disorders are a leading global cause of disability, affecting people of all demographics (age, gender, ethnicity…) and contributing significantly to reduced quality of life, loss of productivity and healthcare costs. The complexity of their pathophysiology across scales eludes healthcare professionals, and treatments remain mostly palliative with predominantly one-size-fits-all approaches. As the concept of digital twins in health develops, in silico modelling and simulation provides unique opportunities to integrate heterogeneous information coherently, for precise stratification and targeted treatment and prevention. However, and despite the broad impact of MSK disorders, the models simulating MSK function and disease remain largely derived from homogeneous data biased, as per sex, age, health status, and ethnics. This lack of diversity limits applications in precision medicine and risks reinforcing systemic healthcare inequities in diagnosis and treatment.The EDI-MSK MSCA Doctoral Network aims to train a new generation of professionals in in silico medicine with expert culture and skills to include diversity at the core of model developments for MSK health and disease, across scales. Specifically, by using data from experiments, and from population and patient cohorts, stratified by sex, age, and co-morbidities, also integrating social sciences and coproduction with communities, the DN will uniquely define diversity hallmarks to be incorporated into MSK models. It will generate and test methodological blueprints to incorporate life habits, sex, including women’s health, age, rare and chronic disease, and ethnicity. The EDI-MSK consortium includes seven beneficiaries and 13 associated partners. It benefits from the experience of non-profit institutions and SME that are significant players in the in silico medicine ecosystem and will make the EDI-MSK Doctoral Candidates become leaders of the transformation of MSK model towards inclusivity.

title: Supporting Parents to Protect Children
objective: Protection and wellbeing of children is at the forefront of policy concerns in Europe. Where children are abused and neglected, states intervene through Child Protection & Welfare systems and services, sometimes resulting in children being placed in out-of-home care.Policy and practice are recognizing the need to support parents in protecting children due to greater knowledge on the role of positive parenting in child development, understanding of the value of prevention and early intervention and the risks to development for children brought up in traditional institutional care settings. While Parenting Support and Child Protection & Welfare are established, separate bodies of research, they are not integrated, with limited, rigorous research spanning both fields.SUPAR (Supporting Parents to Protect Children) will create an ambitious, frontier-breaking, cross-disciplinary, cross-sectoral and international programme of doctoral training and research.  It will create a new group of leaders to progress knowledge creation and policy impact on supporting parents in Child Protection & Welfare services.SUPAR will address intertwined evidence challenges on Parenting Support in Child Protection & Welfare, on cross-sectoral and cross-disciplinary working, and on how policy and law can enable Parenting Support as a strategy to protect children.SUPAR will innovate: by co-producing its research through the participation of those with lived experience of Child Protection & Welfare services across the full research lifecycle; by focusing on all levels of Parenting Support in Child Protection & Welfare from front-line practice to policy; and by embedding cross-disciplinary and cross-sectoral collaboration as a fundamental imperative of its research and training components.SUPAR’s research programme, mirrored in its multi-component doctoral training, will crystallise Parenting Support as a necessary component of Child Protection & Welfare policy and practice.

title: Synergistic Neuromorphic Approaches for Scalable and Efficient Computing
objective: SYNAPSE (Synergistic Neuromorphic Approaches for Scalable and Efficient Computing) addresses one of Europe’s most pressing technological challenges: the need for radically more efficient computing systems in the face of exponential data growth and increasingly AI-intensive applications. As digitalisation accelerates across industry, public services, and society, existing computing architectures—rooted in classical, power-hungry digital designs—are becoming unsustainable, placing constraints on Europe’s competitiveness and energy goals.Neuromorphic computing offers a transformative alternative. Inspired by the brain’s ability to perform complex tasks with unparalleled energy efficiency, neuromorphic systems integrate memory and processing, exploit physical dynamics, and enable adaptive, low-power computation. These capabilities make them uniquely suited to the demands of next-generation AI, edge intelligence, sensing, and cyber-physical systems.The SYNAPSE Doctoral Network brings together leading universities, research institutes, and industrial partners Leonardo, Sony Europe, Imaging Development Systems GmbH, Oriole Networks, E4, AlticeLabs, HIRO-MicroDataCenters to train 15 doctoral candidates (DCs) in the interdisciplinary foundations and applications of neuromorphic technologies. Through a programme spanning photonic and electronic neuromorphic hardware, novel architectures, algorithm–hardware co-design, and application-driven demonstrators, SYNAPSE will equip DCs with the technical expertise, innovation skills, and intersectoral experience needed to shape Europe’s future computing landscape. Through hands-on training and industrial secondments DCs will gain direct experience in addressing real-world challenges.By fostering a new generation of scientific and industrial leaders, SYNAPSE aims to accelerate the deployment of energy-efficient, high-performance computing systems and reinforce Europe’s strategic position in the digital and post-digital economy.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Joint Communication and SENSing in Optical NEtworks
objective: Optical networks are crucial to modern society and the economy, forming the backbone of our advanced communication infrastructure. Currently, these networks are undergoing a transformative phase, driven by the demands – and needs – of increased and everywhere connectivity and real-time data acquisition for monitoring and performance enhancement. Both demands lead to system architectures that have the potential to be exploited in other contexts, thereby leveraging considerable value from the significant costs of installation. In particular, there is the potential to transform the telecommunications network into a globe-spanning distributed sensing system with applications ranging from earthquake, tsunami, and fires detection to infrastructure monitoring.Recent developments in the field highlighted the potential of integrating high-speed optical communication with distributed sensing, offering an ambitious holistic approach to data acquisition, monitoring and analysis. This integration promises to enhance the intelligent functionalities of ubiquitous optical networks, pushing the boundaries of what is achievable with traditional optical communications. The Doctoral Network AI-Sense (Artificial Intelligence for Joint Communication and SENSing in Optical NEtworks) brings together internationally leading teams from academia, start-up Enlightra and global telecom industry players, including Nokia Germany and Portugal, Nokia Networks France, and ADTRAN to train a cohort of 14 DCs in the emerging area of joint optical communication with distributed sensing, incorporating artificial intelligence/machine learning methods for enhanced real-time data collection and analytics. The industrial partners involvement in the project provides DCs access to invaluable resources, expertise, and technologies. AI-Sense has the ambition and the vision to create a new generation of scientific and industrial leaders, strengthening Europe’s competitiveness.

title: Bridging Quantum and Classical Error Correction for Scalable Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing
objective: Quantum computers promise breakthroughs in cryptography, chemistry, materials, optimisation and artificial intelligence. However, their progress is fundamentally limited by errors in fragile quantum hardware. Quantum error correction (QEC) is the key enabling technology to make quantum computing reliable and scalable. Nevertheless, current approaches remain fragmented across disciplines, inefficient, and not yet fully optimised for existing qubit platforms.QuBriC will establish the first European doctoral network entirely dedicated to QEC with the aim of bridging classical coding theory and quantum information science for scalable, hardware-ready QEC. It integrates mature classical error-correction methodologies with quantum information principles into a unified framework covering theory, code design, decoding, hardware integration, and experimental validation. The network is uniquely structured to operate coherently across major qubit platforms, enabling systematic comparison and transfer of concepts. QuBriC brings together 16 leading academic institutions and 7 major quantum computing companies to tackle the key QEC bottlenecks. At its core is an integrated research and training programme that develops doctoral candidates fluent across the full QEC stack. This prepares researchers to operate across disciplines and contribute to hardware-constrained QEC development. Through secondments and joint supervision across 11 countries, doctoral candidates gain direct exposure to diverse academic and industrial workflows in real-world quantum technology environments.Aligned with the Horizon Europe and Digital Decade priorities on digital infrastructure, deep-tech skills and technological sovereignty, QuBriC strengthens Europe’s long-term capacity in fault-tolerant quantum computing. By delivering cross-domain researchers, open tools, training materials and validated methodologies, the network consolidates Europe’s sustainable leadership in quantum technologies.

title: Public Administration Doctoral Network in Digital and Green Transitions
objective: PANDORIS establishes an innovative doctoral training network dedicated to equipping Doctoral Candidates (DCs) with cutting-edge expertise in transformative governance for the twin digital-green transitions. The program addresses a critical knowledge gap by training DCs to navigate and manage the complexities inherent in digital and sustainable transformations, producing specialists skilled in political, societal, and economic facets of twin transition governance. This interdisciplinary, intersectoral network provides robust research, mentorship, and mobility opportunities, ensuring DCs gain versatile skills applicable across academia, public, and private sectors. The project fosters international cooperation among consortium partners, enhancing research capacity and knowledge exchange to build a cohesive approach to public administration and sustainability. By generating evidence-based insights and solutions, PANDORIS aims to influence policy, enrich existing doctoral programs, and extend best practices beyond academia. With a specific focus on the integration of public and private sector innovations, this program advances a comprehensive framework for transformative governance, paving the way for resilient, sustainable public administrations capable of leading Europe’s twin transition.

title: Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies
objective: REGULAIRE is a doctoral network that studies how regulation can learn and adapt in situations where technologies, risks, and expectations change quickly. Good governance depends on strengthening how institutions observe emerging problems, test potential solutions, and update their practices as new evidence becomes available. In fast-moving environments, the capacity of institutions to learn becomes an essential regulatory function. The network will train fifteen fellows to examine this learning process from different angles. They will look at how authorities detect early signals, design and test interventions, evaluate what works, and share findings across organisations. The research is organised into four themes. (1) anticipating emerging issues, (2) improving regulatory tools and processes, (3) assessing institutional capacity, and (4) making learning travel beyond individual pilots. Each project links real-world and timely institutional settings with clear methods such as legal analysis, process tracing, experimental and quasi-experimental evaluation, incident analysis, and evidence synthesis. A shared measurement framework ensures that results are comparable and can build on each other. Fellows will spend time inside regulators, ministries, standard-setting bodies, agencies, industry, and civil society, to ensure that the training is grounded in practice. Together they will create concrete outputs such as guidance, templates, and an open observatory that collects signals, methods, and results from regulatory experiments. By focusing on how regulation learns, REGULAIRE aims to improve the ability of European institutions to update rules in a timely, evidence-based, and proportionate way. This strengthens competitiveness, trustworthiness and protects fundamental rights in an era of rapid technological change.

title: A doctoral training programme for next-generation LUNG-targeted non-viral GENEtic MEDicines
objective: The lungs play a crucial role in breathing and exchanging gases, and are vulnerable to numerous illnesses, including cystic fibrosis, cancer, asthma, and infections. The application of gene-based therapies is a crucial focus in the development of new treatments for these life-threatening conditions. The administration method is crucial for lung targeted genetic therapies: Inhalation stands out as a non-invasive route, providing ease of use, quick action, localized treatment, and fewer side effects compared to intravenous methods. However, despite its advantages, inhaled RNA therapies have yet to gain clinical approval due to challenges in navigating the complex lung environment and ensuring effective gene delivery.In LUNG-GENEMED, we aim to develop advanced delivery systems that effectively penetrate lung barriers—such as mucus, surfactant proteins, and mucociliary clearance—to enhance treatment efficacy while minimizing dosage. We will build up a multidisciplinary network of 11 academic partners and 8 non-academic associated partners with expertise in soft matter, drug delivery, aerosolization, respiratory physiology and physiopathology and organ-on-chip technology. We will recruit and train 13 Doctoral Candidates (DC) for generating highly skilled scientists with competencies at the cutting edge of gene therapy who will spread their acquired knowledge across Europe well beyond the timeframe of this project. The training program will focus on developing tailored genetic nanotherapeutics for lung delivery to target untreatable diseases by elucidating the intricate bio-nano interaction patterns within the lungs. Organ-on-chip models of lungs will be used to test safety and efficacy of therapeutics, while reducing animal testing. Overall, we will tackle the current barriers arresting gene therapy by training the next generation scientists through individual training-through-research projects and secondments, scheduled in both academic and non-academic partners.

title: Functionally Unified, Trustworthy, Ultra-Responsive, Reasoning-Enabled 6G with Autonomous Agents
objective: Federated, Unified, Trustworthy, Ubiquitous Reinforcement-learning Enabled 6G through Agentic AI represents a timely and edge-cutting doctoral network addressing Europe's strategic imperative to lead autonomous 6G intelligence. At a critical moment when global competition for AI-native networking leadership intensifies, FUTURE-6G pioneers the integration of agentic AI systems—combining large language models, reinforcement learning, and multi-agent coordination—to enable zero-touch, self-managing 6G network operations aligned with the EU AI Act. This truly industrial doctorate brings together an exceptional consortium of 11 beneficiary organizations and 11 academic partners spanning world-leading telecommunications infrastructure providers (Nokia, Ericsson, Telefónica, TurkCell, Orange), cutting-edge AI hardware innovators (NVIDIA), semantic technology (ECCENCA, DTC) and RAN integration experts (IQU, ISW), and premier research institutions, creating an unparalleled innovation ecosystem where 15 doctoral candidates work embedded within industrial environments while pursuing rigorous academic training. The 15 DCs conduct research directly aligned with industry-driven challenges—from autonomous RAN orchestration and intent-driven actuation to quantum-resilient network security and energy-efficient edge intelligence—bridging the gap between academic theory and production deployment. Each doctoral researcher gains hands-on experience with production-grade network testbeds, GPU-accelerated HPC infrastructure, advanced digital twin simulation environments, and real operational networks, while contributing breakthrough innovations in agentic orchestration frameworks, hallucination-resilient LLMs, and trustworthy AI reasoning engines. FUTURE-6G delivers European technological sovereignty in AI-native network systems, creating competitive advantages through superior fault management, spectrum efficiency, energy optimization, and autonomous decisions.

title: Empowering Innovation for a Sustainable Plastic Future
objective: The SkillCirc Doctoral Network addresses the critical challenge of transitioning from a linear plastic economy to a circular, sustainable paradigm by advancing eco-plastic technologies and fostering interdisciplinary research. This initiative brings together a multidisciplinary consortium of leading academic and industry partners to train the next generation of researchers capable of driving innovation in plastic reuse, recycling, and sustainability. SkillCirc will train 11 Doctoral Candidates through a holistic program combining rigorous scientific research, hands-on laboratory experience, and engagement with industry and policy actors. Each DC will tackle a critical aspect of the plastic life cycle, from the development of bio-based and indefinitely recyclable polymers to the integration of artificial intelligence for real-time process monitoring and optimization. Innovative approaches such as biocoloring, biocatalytic depolymerization, and eco-polymer film development will pave the way for high-performance, sustainable alternatives to plastics. Alongside technical advancements, SkillCirc will explore the social, economic, and policy dimensions of plastic use, including public attitudes, household practices, and policy narratives, ensuring that innovations are socially embedded and widely adopted. The program employs advanced training methodologies, including interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary approaches, to equip DCs with a diverse skill set. Reflective practice, structured industry placements, and exposure to social scientific perspectives will prepare researchers to bridge the gap between laboratory discoveries and real-world applications. Through collaboration, innovation, and a strong commitment to sustainability, SkillCirc aims to not only revolutionize the lifecycle of plastics but also cultivate the next generation of leaders who will drive transformative change in academia, industry, and policy-making, shaping a greener, more sustainable future.

title: University Network for Industrial Quality, aUtomation, Ecology and Excellence
objective: Europe’s industry must become more sustainable, resilient and digitally advanced, yet traditional efficiency-driven models cannot address climate change, resource scarcity, supply chain risks and rapid technological change. Advances in automation, AI and systems modelling create new opportunities, but real progress requires a shift toward human-centric industrial systems where workers collaborate with digital technologies and social and ethical factors shape innovation. Current doctoral training remains fragmented across digitalisation, circular economy and robotics, with few integrated frameworks linking industrial management, industrial ecology, advanced digital technologies and Industry 5.0 principles.UNIQUE-DN responds by training 12 researchers to develop integrated methods that improve industrial performance while supporting environmental sustainability and worker wellbeing. The network unites leading academic and industrial partners across Europe to deliver research at the intersection of management, ecology, human-centric engineering and digitalisation, supported by cross-sectoral training and international secondments.The ESR projects address circularity-digital integration, cognitive digital twins, sustainable wearable systems, semantic tools for industrial ecology, explainable AI for zero-defect circular manufacturing with Digital Product Passports, Manufacturing-as-a-Service models, sustainability-focused virtual commissioning, AI-based system modelling, human-centred AI maturity, remanufacturing decision tools, adaptive design and digital twins for renewable energy.Through structured work packages, joint supervision and real-world testbeds, UNIQUE-DN strengthens Europe’s capacity for sustainable and human-centred industrial transformation aligned with the Green Deal and Digital Europe priorities.

title: Kernel-based Methods in Control and Estimation
objective: The proposed programme will establish a Doctoral Network in Mathematics with a special focus on Kernel-Based Methods in Control and Estimation. The network aims at advancing the theoretical foundations and practical applications of kernel-based techniques in control and estimation of complex dynamical systems. By bringing together leading researchers and institutions, the project will foster interdisciplinary collaboration and innovation in areas such as state estimation for partial differential equations, data-driven analysis of nonlinear dynamics, and uncertainty quantification in complex systems. The network will also explore the integration of machine learning methods, including physics-informed deep learning and Gaussian process online learning, to enhance control strategies and state estimation in uncertain and nonlinear environments. Additionally, the project will address real-world applications from different technological domains. Furthermore, by incorporating physical prior-knowledge into data-driven control and developing localized sensitivities for efficient learning, the network seeks to create robust, reliable, and efficient methods applicable across various industries. The doctoral network will not only contribute to advancing mathematical knowledge but also strengthen European innovation capacity by training highly skilled researchers equipped to tackle complex mathematical problems. Through collaborative research projects, workshops, and dissemination of findings in top-tier journals and conferences, the network will have a lasting impact on both academia and industry, fostering sustainable development and technological advancement.

title: Training a New Generation to Decode the Human Cis-Regulatory Genome
objective: Decoding how the “non-coding” genome controls gene expression is one of the grand challenges of modern biomedicine. Most disease-associated variants fall in regulatory DNA, yet their effects on gene regulation remain largely unpredictable, limiting diagnosis, risk stratification and the design of safe gene and cell therapies. cisCODE is an MSCA Doctoral Network that will train 15 Doctoral Candidates to crack the cis-regulatory code by combining cutting-edge genomics with artificial intelligence and synthetic biology.The network gathers 13 academic partners, completed with 9 non-academic partners across experimental and computational disciplines. Together, they will (i) decode the sequence “grammar” and modular function of cis-regulatory elements, (ii) map the rules of communication and compatibility between distal enhancers and promoters in three-dimensional chromatin, and (iii) build causal, predictive enhancer-based gene regulatory networks in health, stress, inflammation and cancer. Doctoral projects will leverage single-cell multi-omics, high-throughput functional assays, advanced 3D genome profiling and next-generation AI models to move from descriptive catalogues to mechanistic and predictive understanding.cisCODE is also a training engine for Europe. A structured, international and intersectoral programme will provide Doctoral Candidates with personalised research and career development plans, network-wide schools, secondments in industry and clinics, and dedicated training in open science, data stewardship, ethics and innovation.By delivering new models, datasets and synthetic regulatory tools openly to the community, cisCODE will accelerate interpretation of regulatory variants, support the rational design of precision therapies, and consolidate Europe’s leadership at the interface of regulatory genomics, artificial intelligence and personalised medicine.

title: UNderstanding change in Cultural Heritage: the Next Generation of Experts
objective: Cultural Heritage (CH) objects change over time due to environmental factors, material aging, and past human actions. These changes often invisible until they become irreversible and are difficult to measure, interpret, and predict. As digital technologies, imaging, and data science increasingly influence conservation practices, there is a growing need for researchers and professionals skilled in linking material knowledge, conservation science, advanced imaging, and artificial intelligence.UNCHANGE addresses this need by exploring how and why CH materials change, connecting the physical and chemical causes of deterioration to their visible and invisible effects. The project will develop non-invasive imaging methods, mechanistic models, and computational tools to document, analyze, and forecast changes. These innovations will help create heritage digital twins of heritage objects, enabling better conservation decisions and new ways to visualize their past, present, and future states.As a Doctoral Network, UNCHANGE will train a new generation of researchers capable of working across conservation science, materials science, imaging physics, and AI. Through close collaboration with museums, heritage institutions, and scientific partners, the project will test its methods on representative case studies and promote the digital transformation of the sector. By improving understanding, monitoring, and communication of changes in CH objects, UNCHANGE aims to support more resilient and evidence-based strategies for their long-term preservation.

title: Safe, Thriving and Engaged Pedestrians in Urban Public Spaces
objective: The global objective of STEP-UP is to support 10 DCs in developing into a new cohort of professionals, whose acquired expertise, innovative approaches and interdisciplinary training, will empower them to effectively integrate pedestrian needs into transport research, planning and design, addressing present and future challenges in alignment with global and EU initiatives. It is structured around 3 dimensions: research, training, and outreach & dissemination. A. Advance research towards a more comprehensive understanding of pedestrian behaviour by applying novel interdisciplinary approaches and methodological frameworks, realised through joint supervisory. The research involves 3 objectives. 1. to develop an understanding of the intra- and interpersonal dynamics underlying pedestrian behaviour. 2. to design and evaluate solutions that remove environmental and infrastructural barriers to walking in urban environments. 3. to overcome conflict and integration challenges with other types of road users. Each targets a distinct type of pedestrian interaction towards the formulation of an understanding of pedestrian behaviour, supporting the design of safe, comfortable and inclusive urban public spaces. B.  Advance doctoral training by designing a program that draws on interdisciplinary knowledge and cross-sectoral methods, applies participatory design and offers courses and activities addressing the challenges researchers face today due to the rapid pace of developments in science, professional landscape and society. C. Disseminate results in the academic and scientific community to advance the SoA and contribute to the scholarly development of the next generation of students and professionals. Build connections with researchers, the industry, practitioners to foster a collaborative network aligned with the innovative approaches, perspectives, and understanding of pedestrian needs and behaviour, developed within STEP-UP.

title: Solar-driven hYBrid Methane production via BioelectrOchemicaL CO2 utilization
objective: The SYMBOL Doctoral Network pioneers a new generation of solar-biohybrid technologies for decentralized biomethane production. SYMBOL introduces a Dual Pathway Conversion (DPC) architecture that merges two synergistic CO2-to-CH₄ routes: (i) a biophotoelectrochemical (BPEC) process in which Cu2O-based plasmon-enhanced photocathodes generate H2 in situ for biological methanation, and (ii) a direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) process enabling direct photo-electron uptake by methanogenic archaea without molecular hydrogen. The integrated system achieves hydrogen-free, low-temperature, solar-driven biomethanation from biogenic CO2, fully consistent with the EU Green Deal, REPowerEU and Fit-for-55 objectives.Ten doctoral projects combine frontier research in materials chemistry, electrochemistry, microbiology, photovoltaics, modelling and system engineering, culminating in a validated TRL 3 prototype. Key innovations include self-healing plasmonic Cu2O photocathodes, low-overpotential transition-metal chalcogenide anodes, semi-transparent patterned perovskite solar cells for light-sharing, and advanced membranes enabling stable hybrid operation. Together they target ≥ 5 % solar-to-methane efficiency and ≥ 95 % selectivity under continuous illumination.Beyond scientific excellence, SYMBOL establishes a pan-European doctoral training ecosystem integrating academia and industry (Prodeval, Antares, EBA) through intersectoral secondments, transferable-skills courses, open-science practices, and career mentoring. The programme will train ten highly employable researchers capable of advancing CO2 valorisation and renewable-gas innovation. By coupling cutting-edge technology with structured training, SYMBOL strengthens Europe’s capacity for climate-neutral energy, sustainable process engineering and the circular-carbon economy.

title: AI4Power: Artificial Intelligence for low carbon Power systems
objective: Pressing concerns about climate change impose ambitious targets for energy system decarbonization based on high penetration of renewable energy sources (RES). The energy transition reshapes existing systems, creating both challenges and opportunities, mainly in situational awareness, operational planning and control and power system stability.Artificial intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI) are set to transform power system and smart grid operation by processing large datasets, optimising complex functions and enabling new capabilities. However, despite promising AI and machine-learning (ML) solutions demonstrated in literature and pilots, their potential remains underused due to planners’ and operators’ reluctance to adopt methods they cannot fully understand or trust. Trust, explainability and adaptability thus remain key for AI uptake in this conservative sector.AI4Power aims to deliver innovative AI-based solutions for critical areas of system operation and control, demonstrating trustworthiness, explainability, and adaptability and creating a model for wider AI adoption in power system applications. A further barrier to integrating AI and GenAI is the limited expertise across both AI and energy domains. AI4Power will address this by developing advanced, complementary research skills through a coordinated doctoral training programme, preparing a new generation of researchers skilled in AI technologies and their application in energy systems.

title: Doctoral Training Network on Glycan–Cancer–Microbiota Interactions for Therapeutic and Diagnostic Innovation in Colorectal cancer
objective: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, and increasing evidence shows that gut microbiota plays a decisive role in tumour progression and immune escape. Yet, the molecular rules governing communication between tumour cells, microbes and the immune system remain unknown. GlyCaBiota DN addresses this critical gap by focusing on how tumour and microbial glycans and proteins that recognize them shape CRC biology. Our innovative programme places glycan-mediated interactions at the core of the tumour–microbiota–immune axis, enabling the rational development of next-generation diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. By combining structural, cellular and computational approaches, GlyCaBiota will decode the molecular mechanisms driving microbial colonisation, immune modulation and CRC progression. Our consortium brings together leading experts in glycoscience, microbiology, cancer biology and immunology, structural biology, bioinformatics and translational research. With nine academic and five industrial partners, one oncology center and an international network, GlyCaBiota provides complementary expertise, unique tools and clinical connections to train 15 doctoral candidates (DCs). The combination of excellent interdisciplinary science, industry know-how and clinical perspective covers the entire pipeline from fundamental discoveries to innovative solutions. DCs will gain cutting-edge scientific and transferable skills, positioning them for impactful careers across academia, industry and healthcare. GlyCaBiota will create a critical mass of researchers capable of integrating glycoscience and microbiome research to tackle key challenges in CRC. By deciphering glycan-mediated interactions, GlyCaBiota will expand fundamental knowledge and strengthen European innovation capacity, enabling future development of precision diagnostics and therapeutic strategies for CRC.

title: Science for WInd turbine Resilience to Lightning
objective: Lightning poses significant risks to both ground-based and airborne structures, including their electrical and electronic systems. Wind turbines (WTs) are particularly vulnerable due to their height, the use of modern composite materials, and the increasing integration of sensitive electronic equipment. As wind power becomes a cornerstone of our carbon-neutral future, lightning damage to WTs already costs over €100 million annually worldwide - expected to rise with the expansion of wind farms and advancements in turbine technology. Despite these challenges, fundamental questions remain about lightning initiation, multiscale physical mechanisms, and the processes governing leader attachment to turbine blades.The SWIRL Doctoral Network introduces a multidisciplinary consortium of academic and industrial partners to address these challenges by advancing knowledge and developing innovative solutions for WT lightning protection. The network will deliver a cutting-edge, bespoke doctoral training programme, combining a scientific approach with practical technological applications, SWIRL integrates diverse methodologies, including  multi-instrumental lightning observations in a WT, advanced high-voltage laboratory testing, state-of-the-art computational modelling, and fostering a unique environment for cross-disciplinary collaboration. The network bridges meteorology, electrical discharge physics, materials science, and electrical engineering, enabling researchers to tackle lightning-related challenges at the intersection of these fields. The programme aims to produce the first generation of experts combining such expertise, to ensure the resilience of wind energy systems and other critical infrastructures. With a strong focus on non-academic involvement, SWIRL ensures that researchers gain exposure to industrial challenges while contributing to solutions that directly address sector needs, this way enhancing their career prospects in both academic and industry sectors.

title: Network for Integration of Comb Experimental Spectroscopic Techniques
objective: NICEST is a Doctoral Network dedicated to advancing next-generation optical frequency comb spectroscopy to address pressing scientific and societal challenges in astrochemistry, atmospheric monitoring, and sustainable industrial processes. Molecular processes in gaseous environments govern phenomena ranging from interstellar chemistry to climate-relevant reactions and plasma-assisted manufacturing. Their accurate description requires high-resolution, broadband spectroscopic tools capable of detecting transient species with exceptional precision—capabilities that current instruments only partially achieve.NICEST brings together leading European groups in laser science, precision spectroscopy, molecular physics, plasma and combustion chemistry, and data science, complemented by major industrial partners. The network will train 11 Doctoral Candidates through an integrated program that links instrument development, high-accuracy reference measurements, and applications to complex chemical environments. The consortium will develop broadband, sensitive, and time-resolved spectrometers based on optical frequency combs, generate benchmark molecular data for species of atmospheric and astrophysical relevance, and apply these tools to plasma, combustion, and low-temperature reaction systems.The resulting instrumentation, datasets, and methodological advances will significantly enhance Europe’s capabilities in environmental monitoring, climate-relevant diagnostics, and analysis of astronomical spectra, while supporting innovation in clean technologies and decarbonization strategies. NICEST will form the first European cohort trained to deploy comb-based spectroscopy across scientific and industrial sectors, strengthening long-term skills, interdisciplinary collaboration, and European scientific leadership in precision measurement.

title: Doctoral Training Centre for the Materials Innovators of the Future
objective: The Doctoral Training Centre bridging Advanced Digital Materials Discovery and Advanced Processing Technologies to develop the Materials Innovators of the Future (ADAPT-MIF) will prepare PhD graduates who understand the interplay of diverse cutting-edge materials discovery, processing, and manufacturing techniques. These innovators will be equipped to drive innovation from materials research to products that enhance society and the environment. ADAPT-MIF expands the scope of our established Centre for Doctoral Training in Digital and Automated Materials Chemistry, providing successsful fellows access to a unique inter-disciplinary training program and internationally recognized academic supervisors leading pioneering research worldwide. Recognizing that modern materials innovation demands the fusion of computation and experimentation across scales, ADAPT-MIF will train PhD graduates with expertise in materials chemistry, data science and automation, and advanced processing and manufacturing. Through a cohort-based training approach, ADAPT-MIF brings together international doctoral fellows from physical sciences, computer sciences, and materials and chemical engineering backgrounds. In collaboration with cross-sector industrial partners, the program will develop their core skills in automation, robotics, and artificial intelligence, applied within specific materials design, discovery, formulation, and processing research projects. The state-of-the-art Materials Innovation Factory (MIF) will be home to ADAPT-MIF fellows, providing a world-leading robotic materials synthesis suite and fostering an industrial mindset within an inter-sectoral collaborative research environment that nurtures leadership and entrepreneurial skills.
